item.title: Variational relaxation and gradient flows for degenerate elliptic conductivity problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.33173v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a convex-analytic $L^2$-framework for gradient flows of pumping-energy functionals coupled with elliptic state equations and an evolving nonnegative conductivity $a\geq 0$. The main difficulty is that the conductivity may be merely square-integrable, or degenerate, and formal differentiation need not produce an $L^2$-subgradient. After imposing the strictly positive lower cutoff $r+a\geq r>0$, we define the pumping-energy functional by a variational formula, prove convexity and lower semicontinuity, and show that its $L^2$-subdifferential is nonempty if and only if the pressure gradient belongs to $L^4$. We also obtain a unique maximal-monotone $L^2$-gradient flow satisfying an energy identity. Moreover, we prove Mosco convergence of the pumping-energy functionals as the cutoff vanishes. An inverse-moment conductivity constraint provides a weak alternative to a uniform positive lower bound. For nonlinear laws $a=\mu(b)$, primal and flux representations distinguish two complementary regimes. If $\mu$ is concave, the pumping-energy functional remains convex, and we characterize its $L^2$-subdifferential and the induced gradient flow. If $1/\mu$ is concave, the pumping-energy functional is concave, and therefore its negative is convex. We construct its pointwise gradient flow on a uniformly elliptic box. Admissible stationary points for power laws yield $p$-Laplacian equations with $p>2$ and $1 < p < 2$, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Jan Haskovec, Peter Markowich, Stefano Zampini

item.title: $L^\infty$ blow-up in the fourth-order Jordan-Moore-Gibson-Thompson equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.33213v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the fourth-order Jordan-Moore-Gibson-Thompson equation \bee u_{tttt}+\al u_{ttt}+\bet u_{tt}-\gamma \Del u_{tt}-\del \Del u_{t}-\varrho \Del u=(f(u))_{ttt}+(f(u))_{tt} \eee under homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions in a smooth bounded domain $\Om \subset \R^n$ with $n\leq 3$, where $\al \in \R$ and $\bet,\gamma,\del,\varrho>0$. First, for any suitably regular initial data and assuming that $f\in C^4(\R)$ with $f(0)=0$, we prove that the corresponding initial-boundary value problem admits a unique maximal strong solution $u$ on $(0, \tm)$. Second, by combining three time-integrated formulations with a series of resolvent-regularized energy estimates, we show that gradient blow-up is ruled out in the sense that \be{EE} \tm<\infty \quad\,\, \Rightarrow\quad\,\, \limsup_{t\nearrow \tm}\|u(\cd,t)\|_{L^{\infty}(\Om)}=\infty. \tag{$\star$} \ee Finally, assuming in addition that $f$ is convex and grows superlinearly in the sense that \bee f''(\xi)\geq 0 \;\; \mbox{ for all}\;\;\xi \in\R, \qquad \frac{f(\xi)}{\xi}\rightarrow +\infty\;\;\mbox{ as}\;\; \xi\rightarrow +\infty , \qquad \int_{\xi_{0}}^{\infty}\frac{d\xi}{f(\xi)}<\infty \;\; \mbox{ for some}\;\; \xi_{0}>0, \eee we employ the extensibility criterion (\ref{EE}) to prove that, for a suitable class of initial data, the solution blows up in finite time in the $L^\infty$-norm. To the best of our knowledge, this provides the first rigorous description of finite-time blow-up for a genuinely nonlinear equation of fourth order in time.
item.dc:creator: Tahir Boudjeriou, Filippo Dell'Oro

item.title: Localized Hybrid Analytical-Finite-Element Thermal Modeling for Laser Powder Bed Fusion
item.description: arXiv:2610.33273v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hybrid analytical--finite-element methods support scan-resolved, part-scale thermal simulation of laser powder bed fusion, but their analytical evaluation cost grows as scan-line contributions accumulate. This work develops a space--time localized hybrid formulation that restricts where and how long each contribution is evaluated analytically. Residual terms and boundary conditions derived from the heat equation allow the finite-element correction to account for the thermal effect of contributions removed from the analytical field. The formulation is assessed using a single-line benchmark against an independent full finite-element solution and multiline comparisons with the conventional hybrid formulation. Localization limits the number of analytical contributions retained while maintaining close agreement with the conventional solution. A comparison with uncompensated temporal truncation demonstrates the importance of the residual correction in retaining the thermal effect of removed contributions. In the 500-line case, analytical and total simulation times are reduced by factors of approximately 25.5 and 3.92, respectively, with a relative nodal 2-norm difference of 0.139%.
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Amin Mohammadi Golafshani, Krishnan Suresh

item.title: Consistency in fractional Korn's inequalities on Lipschitz domains
item.description: arXiv:2610.33325v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate fractional analogs of Korn's inequality on bounded Lipschitz domains in several contexts. Constrained and unconstrained inequalities are established; constraints include quotient spaces and spaces incorporating various classes of boundary conditions or volume constraints. We also expand the parameters of integrability for which the inequalities hold. Specifically, a fractional Korn's first unconstrained inequality holds for vector fields in the fractional Sobolev space $W^{s,p}(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^n)$ for all $p \in [1,\infty]$ and all $s \in (0,1)$. In the cases $p = 1$ and $p = \infty$, the inequality has no local analog. We quantify this by investigating the consistency of the inequalities as the differentiability parameter $s \to 1$; the universal constant in the inequality remains stable for $p \in (1,\infty)$ but degenerates for $p \in \{1,\infty\}$. We introduce an explicit $L^p$-bounded projection operator onto infinitesimal rigid motions as a key tool to quantitatively strengthen the inequality.
item.dc:creator: Tadele Mengesha, James M. Scott

item.title: Initial Data Gluing for Asymptotically Hyperbolic Spacetimes
item.description: arXiv:2610.33372v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a new proof of Corvino-Schoen-type gluing, also known as gluing up to linear obstructions, for asymptotically hyperbolic spacetimes satisfying appropriate smallness conditions in arbitrary dimension. The results retrieve and improve on previous known smallness requirements on initial data to conduct such gluing, including the work of Chrusci\'el and Delay. Our technique is highly versatile and well-suited for gluing results in highly anisotropic geometric settings.
item.dc:creator: Aren Martinian

item.title: Rigidity of Convex Entire Solutions to Sum Hessian Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.33397v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the rigidity of convex entire solutions to sum Hessian equations. Using a dimension-lifting identity, we reduce the problem to a standard \(k\)-Hessian equation in one higher dimension. By applying existing rigidity theorems, we prove that every \(C^2\) convex entire solution is a quadratic polynomial for \(2\leq k\leq n\), \(\alpha\geq0\), and a positive constant right-hand side, without any growth assumption at infinity. We also discuss the linear case \(k=1\).
item.dc:creator: Changyu Ren, Xianlu Sun

item.title: Observability Inequalities for Degenerate Schr\"odinger Equations via a Shape Approximation Method
item.description: arXiv:2610.33406v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a two-dimensional Schr\"odinger equation with a boundary degeneracy. More precisely, the diffusion matrix is given by $ A=\operatorname{diag}(1,x_2^\alpha), \alpha\in(0,1)$, so that the partial differential operator degenerates on a portion of the boundary. The main objective is to establish a boundary observability inequality for the corresponding degenerate Schr\"odinger equation. To overcome the difficulties caused by the boundary degeneracy, we introduce a shape design and approximation procedure. By removing a thin neighborhood of the degenerate boundary, we construct a family of uniformly Schr\"odinger equations on perturbed domains. We first investigate the spectral properties of the associated operators and establish the convergence of the approximate problems to the original degenerate problem. We then derive a boundary observability inequality for the uniformly approximating equations and pass to the limit as the thickness of the removed boundary layer tends to zero. This yields a boundary observability inequality for the original degenerate Schr\"odinger equation. Our approach combines spectral analysis, separation of variables, and shape design techniques. By employing multiplier methods for the uniformly approximating problems and passing to the degenerate limit, we establish the boundary observability inequality for the original degenerate Schr\"odinger equation.
item.dc:creator: Dong-Hui Yang, Hongli Sun, Weijia Wu, Yuanzhi Zhou

item.title: Extremals for Trudinger-Moser inequalities via polygonal profiles
item.description: arXiv:2610.33439v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The aim of this paper is to establish the existence of extremal functions for the Trudinger--Moser inequality with logarithmic weights $(-\log |x|)^{\beta}$ in two dimensions throughout the full range $0\le \beta<1$. We also extend recent results on the existence of local maximizers for the Trudinger--Moser functional beyond the critical threshold. Our approach uses polygonal profiles to establish a lower bound uniform in the weight parameter. An explicit thirty-node profile gives the lower bound $\mathrm{TM}_{4\pi}>4.38421793217\,\pi$ for the classical critical supremum on the unit disk, improving on the value $4.3556\,\pi$ obtained in the computer experiments of Carleson and Chang. This lower bound has a purely analytic proof, which uses only elementary inequalities and exact rational arithmetic. Numerical experiments with polygonal profiles of up to $102400$ nodes suggest that this lower bound can be raised to $4.402732044\,\pi$, which improves the recent computational lower bound by Li and Sun.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e Francisco de Oliveira

item.title: Blow-up analysis and compactness for critical Dirac equations on $\mathbb S^n$
item.description: arXiv:2610.33507v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study blow-up and compactness for the critical nonlinear Dirac equation \[ D_{g_0}\psi_i = H_i|\psi_i|^{\frac{2}{n-1}}\psi_i \qquad \text{on }\mathbb S^n,\quad n\ge 3, \] where $g_0$ is the round metric and $H_i\to H>0$ in $C^0(\mathbb S^n)$. Under a first-threshold bound on the critical mass, we prove that every blowing-up sequence has, after passing to a subsequence, a unique blow-up point $p$ satisfying $H(p)=\max_{\mathbb S^n}H$. The rescaled solutions converge to a ground-state Dirac bubble that carries the entire limiting critical mass. Under local uniform $C^1$ bounds on $H_i$, we use the Kelvin transform and a second rescaling to prove that $p$ is an isolated simple blow-up point. We also derive sharp pointwise and gradient estimates in cylindrical coordinates and identify the normalized Green limit. If the coefficients converge in $C^2$ near $p$, the Pohozaev identity yields $\operatorname{Hess}_{g_0}H(p)=0$. Consequently, if a positive $H\in C^2(\mathbb S^n)$ satisfies $\Delta_{g_0}H(p)<0$ at every global maximum, then solutions with critical mass bounded by a level slightly above the first threshold are uniformly bounded in $L^\infty(\mathbb S^n)$. This bound remains uniform under small $C^2$ perturbations of $H$.
item.dc:creator: Ting Li, Zhongwei Tang

item.title: Mass concentration and ground states of Fermi systems in Hartree--Fock model with potentials
item.description: arXiv:2610.33530v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding the onset and mechanism of collapse at critical attractive interaction is a fundamental problem in the variational theory of finite fermionic systems. In this paper, we study this problem within the Hartree--Fock framework under various trapping potentials. By establishing a finite-rank Hartree-type Gagliardo--Nirenberg--Sobolev inequality, we identify a critical threshold $\mathcal{K}^{(N)}$ governing the existence of ground states. We then determine the concentration behavior of ground states as the interaction parameter approaches $\mathcal{K}^{(N)}$. To reveal how the geometry of the trap influences this critical phenomenon, we consider three representative classes of potentials: polynomial-type potentials, ring-shaped potentials, and potentials whose zero set has nonempty interior. For each class, we derive the concentration scale and sharp asymptotics of the least energy. The resulting regimes are qualitatively different, showing that both the location and the rate of concentration are selected by the local geometry of the potential near its minimum set. In contrast to scalar Hartree problems, the nonlocal interaction is coupled here with pairwise $L^2$-orthogonality constraints, and their interplay creates substantial difficulties in the compactness and blow-up analysis.
item.dc:creator: Zhuocheng Li, Yuan-da Wu, Xiaoyu Zeng

item.title: Uniform boundary observability for periodic waves, I: up to the $\varepsilon^{-1}$ eigenvalue scale
item.description: arXiv:2610.33547v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathcal{L}_\varepsilon=-\operatorname{div}(A(x/\varepsilon)\nabla)$ be a scalar divergence-form operator on a bounded $C^3$ domain, where $A$ is symmetric, uniformly elliptic, Lipschitz continuous, and periodic. For initial data spectrally truncated at the eigenvalue level $N$, we establish whole-boundary observability and projected exact controllability, uniformly in the range $N\leq\delta\varepsilon^{-1}$. This extends the cutoff $N\lesssim\varepsilon^{-1/2}$ obtained by Lin and Shen (J. Eur. Math. Soc. 2022). The key input is a two-sided boundary estimate for fixed-width spectral packets of $\sqrt{\mathcal{L}_\varepsilon}$ at frequencies that satisfy $\varepsilon\mu^2\ll1$. Its lower bound combines quantitative Dirichlet corrector estimates with a forcing-stable microscopic boundary Cauchy estimate. Miller's spectral packet criterion and the Hilbert uniqueness method then convert this packet estimate into the corresponding wave results, with constants independent of $\varepsilon$ and $N$.
item.dc:creator: Jun Geng, Shumao Wang, Wei Wang

item.title: Concave entire solutions of the Liouville equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.33571v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every concave entire solution of the Liouville equation $-\Delta u=e^{2u}$ in $\R^n$ is one-dimensional, and we extend the result to a class of general semilinear equations under suitable conditions on the nonlinearity. In dimension two, we also provide a PDE-based proof of the known classification of quasiconcave solutions to planar Liouville solutions, without relying on complex-analytic methods developed in the previous work by Bergweiler-Eremenko-Langley \cite{BEL}
item.dc:creator: Changfeng Gui, Qinfeng Li, Chunhua Wang, Lu Xu

item.title: Multiplicity of weak solutions for mixed variable exponent triharmonic problems with hardy potentials
item.description: arXiv:2610.33576v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper is devoted to the study of a nonlinear boundary value problem driven by a combination of mixed variable-exponent triharmonic operators and a Hardy-type singular potential. Specifically, we consider \[ \begin{cases} -a(x)\,\Delta_{p(x)}^{3}u - b(x)\,\Delta_{q(x)}^{3}u + m(x)\,\dfrac{|u|^{s(x)-2}u}{|x|^{3s(x)}} = \mu f(x,u), & \text{in } \Omega, \\ u = \Delta u = \Delta^{2}u = 0, & \text{on } \partial\Omega, \end{cases} \] where $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^N$ is a smooth bounded domain with $N > 3$. The operators $\Delta_{p(x)}^{3}$ and $\Delta_{q(x)}^{3}$ represent triharmonic operators with variable exponents, creating a framework of nonstandard growth. Under suitable assumptions on the variable exponents $p(x), q(x), s(x)$, the weight functions $a(x), b(x), m(x)$, and the nonlinearity $f(x,u)$, we establish the existence of at least three distinct weak solutions. Our approach is variational, relying on critical point theory for functionals defined on variable-exponent Sobolev spaces. By combining Ricceri's and Bonanno-Marano's abstract three critical points theorems with new Hardy-Rellich inequalities adapted to the variable-exponent setting, we prove our main multiplicity result for small values of the parameter $\mu$. To our knowledge, this work presents the first systematic treatment of sixth-order problems featuring simultaneously mixed variable exponents and Hardy-type singular potentials.
item.dc:creator: Khalid Soualhine, Adnane Belakhdar, Mohamed karim Hamdani

item.title: Asymptotic analysis of Dirichlet problems in supercritically perforated domains via quantification by torsional rigidity
item.description: arXiv:2610.33621v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Dirichlet problem $-\mathrm{div}(A^{\varepsilon}\nabla u^{\varepsilon}) = f$ on varying open sets $D^{\varepsilon}$, with uniformly elliptic coefficients $A^{\varepsilon}$, in the regime where the solutions vanish in the limit for every source. For periodically perforated domains, this is the supercritical regime. We show that the torsional rigidity $T(D^{\varepsilon})$ is the natural normalization: up to a subsequence, $u^{\varepsilon}/T(D^{\varepsilon})$ converges weakly as measures to $kf$ for every continuous source $f$, where $k$ is a nonzero finite measure independent of $f$, which we call the effective measure. The key ingredient is an estimate comparing $u^{\varepsilon}$ with the product of $f$ and the torsion function, whose rate depends on the domains only through $T(D^{\varepsilon})$. We also show that this rate is optimal. No structural assumption on the perforation is needed, and the results hold for relaxed Dirichlet problems. Every nonzero finite measure arises as an effective measure, so the continuity of the source cannot be dropped in general. For rougher sources, we characterize the convergence by a condition on the domains alone, expressed through their torsion functions or, equivalently, their Poincar\'{e} constants. We also prove that the effective measure is local, satisfies optimal two-sided bounds and is monotone with respect to the coefficients, and we study the role of the antisymmetric parts of the coefficients.
item.dc:creator: Naoto Sato

item.title: Improved Global Boundedness Criteria via Refined Bootstrap Estimates for a Quasilinear Chemotaxis-May-Nowak System
item.description: arXiv:2610.33657v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a quasilinear chemotaxis--May--Nowak system with nonlinear diffusion growing at least as $s^{m-1}$ at high densities and derive improved criteria for global existence and uniform boundedness. For the parabolic--elliptic--parabolic system, we establish global boundedness when $m>3-\frac{4}{n}$ for $n\in\{2,3\}$ and when $m>1+\frac{n}{4}$ for $n\ge4$. For the fully parabolic system, the same conclusion holds under $m>1+\frac{n}{4}$ for $n\ge4$. The proof relies on two refined estimates. Weighted space--time control of the nonlinear infection source yields the low-order $L^q$-bounds for the free virus density needed to initiate the bootstrap in the parabolic--elliptic--parabolic case. Subsequently, preserving the product structure of this source in the interpolation argument allows the chemotactic contribution to be absorbed more efficiently by the nonlinear diffusion. These estimates improve the previously known sufficient conditions for global boundedness.
item.dc:creator: Xueli Bai, Fang Li, Suying Liu, Xuxuan Luo

item.title: Global Boundedness and Finite-Time Blow-up for a Quasilinear Chemotaxis--May--Nowak System
item.description: arXiv:2610.33664v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper continues the work of Bai, Li, Liu and Luo \cite{BaiLiLiuLuoPreprint} on a quasilinear chemotaxis--May--Nowak system. We establish global boundedness in three dimensions for both the parabolic--elliptic--parabolic and fully parabolic systems when $m>4/3$. For the former, we construct finite-time blow-up solutions in balls when $n=3$ and $1<m\le4/3$, and when $n\ge4$ and $0<m\le2-2/n$.
item.dc:creator: Xueli Bai, Fang Li, Suying Liu

item.title: Pseudospectral phenomena preventing the analyticity sector of a Ornstein-Uhlenbeck semigroup to be ruled by the spectral angle of its generator
item.description: arXiv:2610.33683v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study elliptic Ornstein-Uhlenbeck operators in $L^2$ spaces with respect to invariant measures. These operators have discrete spectra and generate analytic semigroups. The angle defining the analyticity sector of a Ornstein-Uhlenbeck semigroup is not always equal to the complementary angle of the spectral angle of its generator. In this work, we study the link between these two angles. More specifically, we provide a necessary and sufficient criterion ensuring that they are complementary, and explain how pseudospectral phenomena account for these two angles to fail to be complementary.
item.dc:creator: Karel Pravda-Starov

item.title: Failure of interior $L^p$ estimates for nonlocal elliptic equations with continuous kernels
item.description: arXiv:2610.33689v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $0<\sigma<2$ and $1\leq p<\infty$. We construct a fixed linear nonlocal elliptic operator $L$ and functions $u_m\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^n)\cap L^\infty(\mathbb R^n)$ such that \[ \|u_m\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb R^n)}+\|Lu_m\|_{L^p(B_2)}\longrightarrow0, \qquad \liminf_{m\to\infty}\|(-\Delta)^{\sigma/2}u_m\|_{L^p(B_1)}>0. \] The kernel is symmetric in the increment variable, uniformly elliptic, and satisfies the standard bounds on its first two derivatives in that variable. Its dependence on $x$ has a uniform modulus of continuity of order $(\log(1/r))^{-1/2}$ as $r\downarrow0$. Moreover, $\|Du_m\|_{L^p(B_4)}\to0$ for $\sigma>1$, and these norms remain bounded for $\sigma=1$. Thus the interior $L^p$ estimates for translation-invariant operators do not extend to this class under mere continuity in $x$.
item.dc:creator: Chang Liu

item.title: Finite-Time Blow-Up for Wave Equations with Nonlinear \(p\)-Laplacian Damping
item.description: arXiv:2610.33700v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a wave equation with linear elasticity, nonlinear \(p\)-Laplacian damping acting on the velocity, and a focusing power source in a bounded three-dimensional domain. For \(2<p<r+1\leq6\), we prove finite-time blow-up in the natural energy norm for initial data in \(H_0^1(\Omega)\times L^2(\Omega)\) lying in the unstable potential well below its depth. This includes every nonzero initial state with nonpositive total energy and requires no sign condition on the initial displacement--velocity pairing. For positive initial energy, we establish a sufficient condition for finite-time blow-up involving the \(L^2\) pairing of the initial velocity with a fixed approximation of the initial displacement. The proof combines a shifted displacement multiplier, an auxiliary quantity built from the time integral of the spatial \(L^p\)-norm of the velocity gradient, and a weighted auxiliary functional. Linking the weight parameter to the initial value of the cumulative quantity allows us to absorb the mixed terms in the auxiliary functional estimate. Together with the shifted displacement multiplier, this yields upper bounds for the maximal existence time in both ranges \(2<p\leq3\) and \(p>3\), without assuming \(W_0^{1,p}(\Omega)\) regularity of the initial displacement.
item.dc:creator: Menglan Liao, Mingxue Zhang

item.title: Dirichlet problem on locally finite graphs (revised and extended version)
item.description: arXiv:2610.33703v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study existence and uniqueness of solutions to the vertex-weighted Dirichlet problem on locally finite graphs. Let $B$ be a subset of the vertices of a connected graph $G$. The Dirichlet problem asks for a function whose discrete Laplacian is prescribed on $V\setminus B$ and whose values are prescribed on $B$. Each infinite connected component of $G\setminus B$ is called an end of $G$ relative to $B$. On finite graphs we show that the solution is the limit of an averaging process, with an explicit geometric rate given by the spectrum of the random walk, and is also the limit of the heat flow and the minimizer of an energy functional. On infinite graphs we prove two existence theorems: one with no assumption on vertex degrees, under a finite-width condition and summable data, and one for bounded data on graphs of bounded degree, where the solution is also unique among bounded functions. If there are no ends, the Dirichlet problem has exactly one solution. If there are $l$ ends, the solution set, when nonempty, has dimension at least $l$; each end carries a positive harmonic function vanishing on $B$. Calling an end parabolic when the random walk started in it hits $B$ almost surely, we show that this function can be taken bounded exactly on non-parabolic ends and is necessarily unbounded on parabolic ones, a discrete analogue of a theorem of Li and Tam. Consequently, bounded solutions are unique if and only if every end is parabolic.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: M. Javaheri, Dirichlet problem on locally finite graphs, Discrete Appl. Math. 155 (2007), no. 18, 2496--2506
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Javaheri

item.title: A Necessary and Sufficient Condition for the Existence of Global Smooth Solutions to the One-Dimensional Inviscid Burgers-Vlasov System
item.description: arXiv:2610.33714v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate global smooth solvability for the one-dimensional inviscid Burgers-Vlasov system. For a smooth initial fluid velocity and a nonnegative, compactly supported particle distribution, we establish a sharp necessary and sufficient threshold expressed through the sum of the initial velocity gradient and the initial particle density. The principal difficulty is to control simultaneously the nonlinear steepening of the fluid velocity, the drag coupling, the particle velocity support, and the full hierarchy of derivatives. To overcome it, we introduce a combined gradient-density quantity whose evolution closes along fluid characteristics. Its sign invariance, together with characteristic support estimates and fixed-order derivative bounds, yields global continuation whenever the initial threshold is nonnegative. If the threshold fails at one point, a Riccati comparison gives an explicit finite upper bound for the maximal smooth lifespan and identifies negative velocity-gradient blow-up when this bound is attained. We also use nonnegative regularization and compactness to extend the threshold result to initial data of any fixed finite regularity.
item.dc:creator: Chengfeng Ren, Huimin Yu

item.title: Variational Structure of Energy-Balance Climate Models with Heterogeneous Insolation
item.description: arXiv:2610.33797v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We analyse stationary Sellers-type energy-balance climate models with heterogeneous insolation $Q_\varepsilon = Q_*+\varepsilon Q_1$, both on the interval $(-1,1)$ with degenerate diffusion $\kappa(x)=1-x^2$ and on $\mathbb{S}^2$ with uniformly elliptic diffusion. Assuming that the homogeneous model corresponding to $\varepsilon = 0$ admits three constant equilibria $\theta_S <\theta_M < \theta_W$ satisfying suitable non-degeneracy and spectral conditions, we prove that, for sufficiently small $\vert \varepsilon \vert $, these equilibria continue to three stationary branches $ u_S^\varepsilon$, $u_M^\varepsilon$, and $u_W^\varepsilon$. The cold and warm branches, $u_S^\varepsilon$ and $u_W^\varepsilon$ respectively, are strict local minimisers of the associated energy functional, while the intermediate branch $u_M^\varepsilon$ is non-degenerate and has Morse index one. We further establish the Palais-Smale condition and obtain a mountain-pass critical point $u^\varepsilon_{MP}$ at the minimax level between the two local minima. Under an additional isolation assumption for the homogeneous problem at the minimax level, this critical point coincides with $u_M^\varepsilon$. Lastly, a Legendre-Galerkin discretisation of the one-dimensional model numerically illustrates the three stationary branches, their discrete Morse indices, and the corresponding energy landscape.
item.dc:creator: Gianmarco Del Sarto, Giuseppe Floridia

item.title: Optimal Control of the 2D Boussinesq Equations with Finite Codimension Constraints
item.description: arXiv:2610.33828v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study an optimal control problem (OCP) governed by the two-dimensional (2D) Boussinesq equations, where the right-hand sides of the velocity and temperature equations are projected onto the corresponding tangent spaces of the manifolds $\mathcal{M}_1:=\{y\in\mathbb{H}:\|y\|_{\mathbb{H}}=1\}$ and $\mathcal{M}_2:=\{\theta\in H:\|\theta\|_H=1\}$, respectively. The resulting evolution is subject to finite-codimensional constraints, under which the state $(y,\theta)$ remains on $\mathcal{M}:=\mathcal{M}_1\times\mathcal{M}_2$ throughout the time interval. A Faedo--Galerkin construction provides a unique, global, strong solution to the constrained Boussinesq system for external controls $\mathfrak{H}\in L^2(0,T;\mathbb{H})$, along with uniform energy bounds. In addition, we establish the existence of an optimal triplet $(y^*,\theta^*,\mathfrak{H}^*)$ that minimizes the quadratic cost subject to the constrained Boussinesq system. Necessary conditions of the first order are obtained through a coupled state--adjoint--control system. The optimal state $(y^*,\theta^*)$ remains on $\mathcal{M}$, while the optimal control lies in the tangent space: $\mathfrak{H}^*(t)\in T_{y^*(t)}\mathcal{M}_1$, for all $t\in[0,T]$. We also show that the map $\mathfrak{H}\mapsto(y_{\mathfrak{H}},\theta_{\mathfrak{H}})$ in $(C([0,T];\mathbb{H})\cap L^2(0,T;\mathbb{V}))\times(C([0,T];H)\cap L^2(0,T;V))$ is Fr\'echet differentiable. The linearized state is the unique weak solution to the constrained linearized Boussinesq system and satisfies the necessary tangency condition. Hence, the well-posedness and first-order optimality conditions are established for the Boussinesq system under nonlinear manifold constraints.
item.dc:creator: Utpal Manna, Manil T. Mohan, Sangram Satpathi

item.title: Well-posedness of the Burgers' equation on the half-line through the Cole-Hopf transformation
item.description: arXiv:2610.33886v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We rigorously establish the well-posedness of the initial-boundary value problem (IBVP) for the Burgers' equation on the half-line for data in Sobolev-type spaces. The formal solution to this problem was previously derived via the Cole-Hopf transformation and the Fokas unified transform method under the assumption of smooth, Schwartz-class data. In this work, we prove the validity of this formal representation for initial data $u_0\in \tilde{H}^{s+1}_x (0,\infty)$ and boundary data $g_0 \in H_t^{{(2s+1)}/{4}}$ where $1/2<s<3/2$. Well-posedness is established under two complementary conditions: (1) sufficiently small initial and boundary data, and (2) non-positive boundary data of arbitrary size. The latter condition utilizes the strong minimum principle for the corresponding linear heat equation to ensure the global invertibility of the nonlinear Cole-Hopf map. The proofs combine linear estimates for the heat IBVP with nonlinear bounds obtained through Taylor series representations and the algebraic properties of Sobolev spaces.
item.dc:creator: Huy K. Vo, Athanassios S. Fokas

item.title: Recovery of a source of anomalous diffusion from space-time sparse data
item.description: arXiv:2610.33896v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study an inverse source problem for a time-fractional sub- and super-diffusive anomalous diffusion equation on the unit disk with sparse boundary observations. We prove the recovery of a general class of $L^2$ sources for anomalous diffusion, with separated variables, from boundary measurements that are sparse in both space and time, using observations at two carefully chosen boundary points on a discrete set of times arbitrarily close to the final time. The analysis relies heavily on the memory effect of the model, properties of complex analysis and the representation of solutions.
item.dc:creator: Xing Cheng, Bangti Jin, Yavar Kian, Zhiyuan Li

item.title: A remark on the global minimality of the cracktip
item.description: arXiv:2610.33900v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a short proof that the planar cracktip is a global minimizer of the Mumford--Shah functional, based on interior and Dirichlet boundary regularity. We construct a Dirichlet minimizer with nonempty discontinuity set and show that this set contains no simple closed curves. The regularity results then imply the existence of an interior regular loose end, at which a blow-up yields the cracktip.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Deangelis, Camillo De Lellis, Matteo Focardi

item.title: Dynamic Interpolation and Higher-Order Turbulence Scales in 3D Navier-Stokes Flows
item.description: arXiv:2610.33911v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the three-dimensional unforced Navier-Stokes equations through the interaction between spatial analyticity and the geometric sparseness of regions of intense fluid activity (i.e., regions where the fluid's motion varies sharply). Interpreting higher-order derivative ratios as turbulence scales, we introduce time-weighted bridge inequalities that quantify the relationship between lower- and higher-order derivative norms. The time weights give the derivative ratios greater flexibility while ensuring that the resulting lower bound on the radius of analyticity dominates the sparseness scale of the super-level sets, indicating that the flow has entered the dissipation regime. Combining this scale comparison with a harmonic-measure maximum principle on one-dimensional sparse sets yields a contraction in the relevant derivative norm, thereby excluding a class of strongly turbulent blow-up scenarios. Consequently, the strong solution extends analytically beyond the candidate blow-up time.
item.dc:creator: Moses Patson Phiri, Zoran Gruji\'c

item.title: Asymptotic stability of transonic steady nozzle flows
item.description: arXiv:2610.33951v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the present article, we prove the nonlinear asymptotic stability of stationary solutions to the quasi-one-dimensional barotropic Euler equations in a finite-length nozzle with variable cross-sectional area $A(x)$. We consider all stationary flow configurations arising from subsonic inflow: flows that remain subsonic throughout the nozzle, flows that pass continuously through a sonic state and remain supersonic up to the exit, and flows that subsequently return to the subsonic regime through a stationary shock. We prove that all these stationary solutions are asymptotically stable with respect to sufficiently small perturbations. No smallness restrictions are imposed on the mass flux, the magnitude of $A_x$, or the prescribed exit pressure, provided that the corresponding stationary solution exists. The only geometrical assumptions are that $A_{xx}>0$ at a smooth subsonic--supersonic transition, and $A_x>0$ at a stationary supersonic--subsonic shock. To the best of our knowledge, this gives the first nonlinear asymptotic stability result for a stationary flow passing smoothly from the subsonic to the supersonic regime in a finite-length nozzle. The principal analytical difficulty is the degeneracy of the characteristic structure at the sonic point. We overcome this difficulty by coupling energy structures adapted respectively to the subsonic and supersonic regimes. This coupling provides the dissipation needed to control the smooth sonic transition, and when combined with the dynamics of the shock, yields a unified nonlinear stability framework for smooth and discontinuous transonic nozzle flows.
item.dc:creator: Masashi Ohnawa, Masahiro Suzuki

item.title: Global $c^{1,\alpha}$ regularity and fine behavior at critical points for quasilinear elliptic equations with Orlicz growth and unbounded drift
item.description: arXiv:2610.33961v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the global regularity up to the boundary and the fine pointwise behavior along the critical set for bounded weak solutions to general quasilinear elliptic Dirichlet problems in Orlicz-Sobolev spaces. Our structural framework encompasses operators with non-standard Lieberman-type growth alongside lower-order terms featuring natural gradient growth, an unbounded source term in $L^q$, and an unbounded spatial drift weight in $L^s$. To overcome the analytical obstructions posed by the unbounded drift across the anisotropic growth gap, we first establish global H\"older continuity up to the boundary via Moser iteration. We then construct a novel smooth regularization scheme for general homogeneous constant-coefficient operators, merging the approximation frameworks of Lieberman and Cianchi-Maz'ya, to derive global $C^{1,\alpha}$ regularity up to the boundary through a variational perturbation approach. Building upon this global theory, we employ a geometric compactness and blow-up argument to prove that at any interior or boundary critical point where the gradient vanishes, the solution achieves an improved pointwise $C^{1,\alpha}$ regularity. Remarkably, at boundary critical points, this quantitative improvement decouples from the lower-order terms and completely bypasses both the boundary datum regularity and the domain smoothness. Finally, we discuss the sharpness of the integrability threshold required for the unbounded drift weight in the subcritical regime.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e Erivamberto Lima Oliveira

item.title: Swirl ill-posedness for incompressible fluids in (sub)critical spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.33973v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For the 3D Navier-Stokes equations with sufficiently smooth initial data having zero swirl $u_{0\theta}\equiv 0$, Ladyzhenskaya \cite{L1968} and Ukhovskii and Yudovich \cite{UY1968} established global regularity. It has since remained open as to whether well-posedness still holds for smooth axisymmetric initial data, with the initial swirl being smaller than an \textit{absolute} constant in a critical space. In this remark, we prove \textit{norm inflation} occurs for the Navier-Stokes scalar swirl component, with initial smallness in the critical space $\dot{H}^{\frac{1}{2}}$ or even subcritical Sobolev spaces. We also obtain norm inflation for the 3D Euler swirl \textit{vector} in the Euler subcritical space $\dot{H}^3$. Our results are achieved by introducing an anisotropic scale in Luo's supercritical norm inflation construction \cite{Luo24}, as well as performing an anisotropic bootstrap argument to get a sufficiently small swirl remainder term.
item.dc:creator: Tobias Barker, Ruilin Hu

item.title: Transport by rough vector fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.33993v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Cauchy-Lipschitz theorem guarantees that the ODE $\dot\gamma = b(t,\gamma)$ is well-posed if $b$ is Lipschitz in space, an assumption too restrictive for applications such as fluid mechanics. In 1989, DiPerna and Lions extended the theory to Sobolev vector fields with bounded divergence. Well-posedness then holds not for individual trajectories but for regular Lagrangian flows: flows that solve the ODE for almost every initial point and compress volume by at most a bounded factor. Their method rests on renormalized solutions of the associated transport equation. This thesis is primarily expository: it presents the DiPerna-Lions theory with detailed proofs. We treat existence, uniqueness and stability of weak and renormalized solutions of the transport equation, deduce existence (for autonomous fields) and uniqueness of regular Lagrangian flows, and discuss applications to the two-dimensional Euler equations. Three counterexamples with divergence-free fields show that uniqueness can fail without a growth condition at infinity, if $b$ has only fractional Sobolev regularity (due to DiPerna and Lions), or for $L^1$ solutions when $\nabla b \in L^r$, $r<d$ (the simplest case of a recent construction by Bru\`e, Colombo and Kumar). Contributions are (1) smooth approximations of $b$ with uniformly bounded divergence for the existence proof; (2) a direct proof of the known uniqueness of regular Lagrangian flows from uniqueness for the continuity equation; (3) a construction of the auxiliary cube-translating field in the example of Bru\`e, Colombo and Kumar that works for all $d \ge 2$, replacing an extension from two dimensions that is not a vector field on $\mathbb R^d$ for $d \ge 3$.
item.dc:creator: Finn Rudolph

item.title: A variational model with finite carrying capacity for segregated multi-species populations in the whole Euclidean space
item.description: arXiv:2610.33996v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a variational problem motivated by models of multiple segregated species in a nonhomogeneous environment. The analysis combines tools from potential theory, in particular free boundary methods. The main novelty is that we formulate the variational problem in the whole Euclidean space while imposing a finite carrying capacity constraint, which allows us to investigate saturated regions where the species attain their maximal density. In addition, we provide a modeling interpretation of the constrained energy. We show that it arises as the variational limit of energies with increasingly strong crowding and interspecific competition penalties, in the sense that, regardless of their relative rates, every sequence of minimizers of the penalized energies admits a subsequence that converges strongly to a minimizer of the constrained energy.
item.dc:creator: Pu-Zhao Kow, Chang-Hong Wu

item.title: Uniqueness of radial bound states for an equation with an odd cubic-like nonlinearity
item.description: arXiv:2610.34025v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate radial bound states with prescribed nodes for the odd cubic equation \[ \Delta u+u(\abs{u}-b)(c-\abs{u})=0 \quad\text{in }\R^n,\qquad n\ge2,\quad 0<b<c. \] Writing $a=b/c$, we prove that a radial bound state with exactly $k\ge1$ simple zeros and positive central value exists if and only if $0<a<1/2$. For each $k$, this solution is unique for all $0<a<1/2$ in dimension two, for $a\ge(7-3\sqrt5)/2$ in dimension three, and for $a\ge(43-5\sqrt{33})/32$ in dimension four. For one node, we identify exact ranges obtained from a tangent comparison and a quotient inequality in every dimension $n\ge3$; the threshold is dimension-independent for $3\le n\le23$ and is characterized implicitly for $n\ge24$. These results address the natural odd counterpart of the cubic nonlinearity highlighted in Tang's prescribed-node uniqueness conjecture [M. Tang, \emph{Invent. Math.}, 2026]. The main challenges are the second positive zero of the cubic source, the lack of a global comparison inequality, and supercritical cubic growth in higher dimensions. We overcome them by an amplitude confinement argument, controlled extensions preserving sharp comparison estimates, and a subcritical truncation for existence. A complementary small-$a$ uniqueness range in dimensions three to five follows from a recent massive double-power result.
item.dc:creator: Wenjing Chen, Zexi Wang

item.title: A superprocess model for eDNA transport in random river environment
item.description: arXiv:2610.34048v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Environmental DNA (eDNA) is increasingly used to monitor aquatic organisms in rivers, yet predicting its concentration and assessing the reliability of such predictions remain challenging because river flow fluctuates with long memory and models of eDNA dynamics are inevitably misspecified. We propose a stochastic modeling framework for eDNA concentration in rivers that addresses both issues. The eDNA concentration is described by a stochastic partial differential equation with transport, decay, source, and square-root multiplicative noise, and the flow velocity is modeled by a superposition of Ornstein-Uhlenbeck-type processes with long memory. We show that the long memory of the flow velocity induces superdiffusive transport of eDNA, with the variance of the transported distance growing superlinearly in the ensemble sense. The proposed model admits a closed-form Laplace functional, based on which we prove the existence and uniqueness in law of the solution on an unbounded domain. We further evaluate the effects of model uncertainty through a robust control formulation based on the relative entropy, in which the lower and upper bounds of the expected eDNA concentration, together with the worst-case distortions, are obtained in closed form. The framework is applied to eDNA and flow velocity data collected for the upstream migration of Plecoglossus altivelis altivelis in a river in Japan. The results demonstrate that the closed-form bounds provide a computationally inexpensive tool for quantifying the range of eDNA concentrations that can be expected under model uncertainty.
item.dc:creator: Hidekazu Yoshioka, Motoh Tsujimura, Ayumi Hashiguchi

item.title: The Dirac Equation in the Classical Limit: A Duality Approach to a Convergence Rate
item.description: arXiv:2610.34086v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the semiclassical limit of the Dirac equation with external electromagnetic fields using a dual formulation based on a Wasserstein-1-type distance. This distance is tailored to matrix-valued density operators and matrix-valued Wigner measures and extends earlier metrics comparing density matrices with classical phase-space distributions in the scalar case. We prove a quantitative convergence rate in the semiclassical parameter, improving previous results for the Dirac equation. Our approach relies on a Lagrange-multiplier formulation of the semiclassical limit for the full matrix-valued Wigner equation (without projection onto energy eigenspaces), introduced in [F. Golse, N. Leopold, N. Mauser, J. M\"oller, C. Saffirio, J. Math. Pures Appl., (2026)].
item.dc:creator: Fran\c{c}ois Golse, Jakob M\"oller

item.title: Lie symmetry analysis of the Saint--Venant equations with variable bottom
item.description: arXiv:2610.34129v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The aim of this paper is to apply Lie-symmetry methods to the one-dimensional Saint--Venant shallow-water equations over variable bottom topography. We classify the bottom profiles that admit symmetry extensions, derive similarity reductions to ordinary differential equations, and analyze selected reduced systems. In particular, heteroclinic trajectories yield physically meaningful self-similar solutions describing the draining and filling of water over a quadratic bottom with a fixed shoreline.
item.dc:creator: Faruk G\"ung\"or, Cihangir \"Ozemir, Pedro J. Torres

item.title: On the Isoperimetric Inequality for the Third Robin Eigenvalue on Surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.34134v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the third Robin eigenvalue on simply connected domains of area $A$ in surfaces with Gaussian curvature bounded above by $K$. For $K>0$, we discover a transition at the critical parameter $\alpha=-4\pi+KA$: two equal geodesic disks give a sharp upper bound when $\alpha=-4\pi$ or $-4\pi+KA\leq\alpha\leq4\pi$, but the two disk bound fails for $-4\pi<\alpha<-4\pi+KA$. In the latter range, we establish a new upper bound involving a single geodesic disk with a modified Robin parameter and prove its sharpness in an explicit subrange. The sharp two-disk inequality persists for nonpositive curvature bounds, and Steklov--Helmholtz analogues are also obtained. Both the two-disk and one-disk bounds arise from a unified two-pole Green-function method, with the one-disk regime emerging from a degenerate area split that produces the $2\pi$ shift in the effective Robin parameter, while sharpness in the stated subrange is established by boundary oscillations that redistribute Robin boundary mass.
item.dc:creator: Xiaoliang Wang, Zuoqin Wang

item.title: Hydrodynamics for hypersingular interactions by $\Gamma$-convergence of gradient flows
item.description: arXiv:2610.34136v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the dynamics of $N$ particles with Riesz repulsive interaction in one dimension, focusing in particular on the hypersingular case (i.e. inverse power with power larger than or equal to the dimension). We prove convergence of the empirical measure to the solution of a porous medium equation by the method of $\Gamma$-convergence of gradient flows introduced by Sandier and the second author. This improves on the prior convergence result by Oelschl\"ager obtained under more stringent assumptions. The method also works for the case where the power is smaller than the dimension, as well as for a class of convex short-range interactions. The proof highlights the crucial role played by the convexity of the interaction, which allows one to show that no excess energy can arise along the flow, implying the needed "slope inequality".
item.dc:creator: Colin McSwiggen, Sylvia Serfaty

item.title: Asymptotic behavior of solutions of the compressible MHD equations on the half space
item.description: arXiv:2610.34166v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the global well-posedness and large-time asymptotic behavior of strong solutions to the $n$-dimensional ($n\ge 2$) compressible viscous resistive magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) equations in the upper half-space $\mathbb{R}_+^n$. We impose the standard no-slip boundary condition on the velocity field and two types of physically relevant boundary conditions on the magnetic field: the insulating boundary condition and the perfectly conducting boundary condition. Under the assumption that the initial data are small perturbations of the constant equilibrium state $(\bar{\rho}, \mathbf{0}, \mathbf{0})$, we first establish the global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions in Sobolev spaces by deriving uniform energy estimates and using a bootstrapping argument. Then, by combining the sharp decay estimates of solutions to the corresponding linearized system with Duhamel's principle, we obtain the decay rates of solutions to the nonlinear problem. Specifically, we prove that the solutions decay at the rate $t^{-\frac{n}{2}\left(1-\frac{1}{p}\right)}$ in $L^p$ norm for $2\le p\le\infty$, and we also establish the decay rates of their first-order derivatives. Furthermore, we show that the global solutions converge to the linearized solutions with an improved decay rate as time goes to infinity. Our results extend the classical results of Kagei and Kobayashi \cite{Kagei-Kobayashi2002, Kagei-Kobayashi2005} for the compressible Navier--Stokes equations on the half space to the compressible MHD system with both insulating and perfectly conducting boundary conditions.
item.dc:creator: Song Gao

item.title: Time-asymptotic expansion and fluid approximation of the 1D Boltzmann equation with hard potentials
item.description: arXiv:2610.34174v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a quantitative large-time comparison between the macroscopic Boltzmann solution and the full nonlinear compressible Navier-Stokes solution in one space dimension. For Maxwellian molecules and hard potentials with angular cutoff, we consider small, spatially compactly supported perturbations of a global Maxwellian with polynomial velocity decay, without assuming spatial differentiability. Nonlinear diffusion waves persist at leading order, making comparison through linearized equations alone insufficient. We construct a coupled system for the leading nonlinear fluid waves and derive cancellation identities from the exact kinetic spectral representation to control interactions between distinct characteristic families. Combined with a particle-fluid decomposition, these yield pointwise estimates separating the leading waves, their interactions, and a faster-decaying remainder.
item.dc:creator: Hui-Tzu Chang, Haitao Wang, Kung-Chien Wu

item.title: Orbital stability of positive standing waves to the logarithmic Choquard equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.34200v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The paper concerns the orbital stability of positive standing waves for the logarithmic Choquard equation with a small local nonlinear perturbation. First, the uniqueness and nondegeneracy of the positive ground-state solution are established via bifurcation and compactness arguments. Then, by exploiting the spectral properties of the linearized operator around the positive ground-state solution in high-energy spaces, the orbital stability of the corresponding positive standing wave is proved. The main difficulty in establishing orbital stability stems from the fact that the logarithmic convolution kernel is both sign-changing and strongly singular, while the norm used to prove global existence is not translation invariant. Consequently, existing approaches to orbital stability for positive ground-state solutions of three-and higher-dimensional Choquard equations with Riesz-type kernels cannot be applied to the two-dimensional logarithmic Choquard equation considered here.
item.dc:creator: Zhisu Liu, Shu-Ming Sun, Weinian Zhang

item.title: Almost global existence for quadratic Schr\"odinger equations in two dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.34237v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the two-dimensional quadratic Schr\"odinger equation $(i\partial_t+\Delta)u=\lambda_1u^2+\lambda_2\overline u^{\,2}$ with initial data of size $\varepsilon$ in a weighted $H^2$ space. We prove almost global existence, with a lifespan of at least $\exp(c/\varepsilon)$ and decay at the optimal linear dispersive rate $t^{-1}$. Our proof is based on the space--time resonance method introduced by Germain, Masmoudi, and Shatah. The main new ingredient is a Besov-type profile norm $\mathcal Z$, which allows us to close the bootstrap argument without controlling the global second spatial momentof the free profile, thereby avoiding the substantial time-dependent losses arising from direct second-moment estimates.
item.dc:creator: Xuan Liu

item.title: Blow-up, critical norm inflation, and global well-posedness for the Geng--Xue system
item.description: arXiv:2610.34267v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study finite-time blow-up, critical norm inflation, and global well-posedness for the Geng--Xue system, an integrable two-component extension of the Novikov equation. For initial velocities $(u_0,v_0)\in(H^s)^2$, $s>3/2$, with second momentum $n_0=v_0-v_{0,xx}\in L^1_{\rm uloc}$, we derive explicit blow-up conditions and upper bounds on the lifespan. The blow-up proof uses a cancellation in the equation for $nu_x$ to close the convolution estimates without an a priori bound on $\|u_x\|_{L^\infty}$. Combined with a continuation criterion involving only $u$, these estimates yield critical Besov norm inflation around the initial data in $(H^{3/2})^2$. For initial momenta in $(H^\sigma)^2$, $\sigma>-1/2$, each with a fixed sign, we prove global well-posedness. The blow-up and norm-inflation results also extend to the three-component Degasperis--Procesi system.
item.dc:creator: Song Liu, Zhaoyang Yin

item.title: Robust Observability for Schr\"odinger Equations with Singular Potentials on 2D Compact Hyperbolic Surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.34287v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the robustness of quantum observability on compact hyperbolic surfaces subject to $L^q$ potential perturbations with $2<q\leq \infty$. Since $L^q$ regularity is strictly subcritical in dimension two, for every non-empty open set $\Omega\subset M$ and $T>0$, the solution of $(i\partial_t+\Delta-V)u=0$ satisfies the space-time observability estimate $$ \|u_0\|_{L^2(M)}^2 \leq C\int_0^T \|e^{-it(-\Delta+V)}u_0\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2\,dt. $$ A cornerstone of our analysis is Sogge's spectral cluster estimate, which allows us to obtain refined spectrally localized semiclassical Strichartz estimates adapted to rough potentials and to show that the potential's contribution vanishes in the propagation of semiclassical measures. The full-support property of invariant semiclassical measures on hyperbolic surfaces associated with the eigenfunctions then yields the desired observability by contradiction. By the Hilbert Uniqueness Method, the corresponding internal controllability result follows.
item.dc:creator: Jiayan Wu, Ting Zhang, Ruze Zhou

item.title: Global Stability of the Kolmogorov--Zakharov Spectrum for the Wave Kinetic Equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.34359v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove global nonlinear stability near the mass Kolmogorov--Zakharov spectrum $f_M(\omega)=\omega^{-7/6}$ for the isotropic cubic wave kinetic equation, including small time-dependent external forces. For sufficiently small initial perturbations and forcing, the solution remains uniformly close to $f_M$ for all time in a weighted norm. This norm allows $f(t,\omega)\sim a_0(t)\omega^{-7/6}$ as $\omega\to0$ and $f(t,\omega)\sim a_\infty(t)\omega^{-7/6}$ as $\omega\to\infty$. When the external force $\phi$ is independent of time, the solution converges at an algebraic rate to a stationary solution in weaker weighted norms. We also give a necessary and sufficient condition on the initial perturbation for convergence in the original weighted norm. These results resolve, for small perturbations of the Kolmogorov--Zakharov spectrum, the question of convergence to a stationary solution under time-independent forcing raised by Collot, Dietert, and Germain (arXiv:2208.00947, Section 1.3). To establish this stability, the collision integral is expanded around $a_0(t)f_M$ at low frequencies and $a_\infty(t)f_M$ at high frequencies, separating it into a linear term with time-dependent coefficients and a nonlinear remainder. This decomposition yields improved control of the nonlinear remainder. The main difficulty is that $a_0(t)$ may vary in time, so the linear operator itself changes with time and its evolution cannot be represented by the semigroup of a single fixed operator. To address this difficulty, we use a parametrix construction to explicitly construct the evolution operator $U_{a_0,a_\infty}$ and establish the required uniform bounds. Moreover, our arguments provide a general framework for proving global stability that may also apply to other evolution equations.
item.dc:creator: Jiajun Wang

item.title: Global Strong Solution to Multi-Dimensional Compressible Quantum Navier-Stokes Equation in Bounded Domains with Large Initial Data
item.description: arXiv:2610.34394v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the compressible quantum Navier-Stokes (QNS) system in a smooth bounded domain, supplemented with a curvature Navier-slip boundary condition for the velocity and a homogeneous Neumann boundary condition for the density. For arbitrarily large initial data away from vacuum, we establish the global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions when the adiabatic index \[ \gamma\in[1,\infty)\quad\text{for }N=2, \qquad \gamma\in\left[1,3\right)\quad\text{for }N=3. \] The argument relies on the effective velocity $v=u+\nabla\log\rho$, which reveals the parabolic structure of the system. Compared with previous works in the periodic and Cauchy cases, additional difficulties arise from the treatment of boundary terms. We also use a bootstrap argument between the density integrability and the weighted integrability of the effective velocity to enlarge the admissible range of $\gamma$ from $\left[1,11/4\right)$ to $\left[1,3\right)$. Combining this bootstrap argument with a De Giorgi iteration for the density upper bound and a Nash-Moser type iteration for the positive lower bound, we derive a priori estimates on every finite time interval and extend the local strong solution globally in time. As far as we know, this is the first result on global strong solutions with large initial data for the initial-boundary value problem (IBVP) of the QNS system in bounded domains with compatibility boundary conditions.
item.dc:creator: Jiaxu Li, Boqiang L\"u, Huixiang Zhou

item.title: Positive solutions of Yamabe-type equations with general potentials
item.description: arXiv:2610.34417v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $(M^n,g)$ be a smooth closed connected Riemannian manifold of dimension $n\ge3$, and let $\psi\in C^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$. We prove that the equation $$ -\frac{4(n-1)}{n-2}\Delta_g u+\psi u=u^{\frac{n+2}{n-2}} $$ has a smooth positive solution if and only if its linear part has positive first eigenvalue. In dimensions $n\ge6$, the proof combines an energy estimate under exact local mass constraints with an intersection argument for finite cycles of atomic measures; dimensions $3\le n\le5$ follow from the theorem of Bahri and Brezis.
item.dc:creator: Hongyu Chen, Li Ma

item.title: An Alt-Caffarelli problem for elastic graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.34447v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study an Alt-Caffarelli-type free boundary problem for symmetric elastic graphs with fixed boundary height. Our results concern existence of minimizers and their description in terms of regularity and shape. It turns out that the weight coefficient in front of the measure term is decisive for existence. We identify a sharp threshold for this coefficient below which existence is guaranteed. Moreover, we find that all sign-changing minimizers are described by a system of three Eulerian elasticae, none of which are lines. Another result shows non-flatness of free boundary points, a classical question in the study of Alt-Caffarelli problems. These properties lead to a better understanding of the nonexistence phenomenon above the aforementioned weight threshold.
item.dc:creator: Marius M\"uller

item.title: Regularity of the solution map for the Oldroyd--B model with fractional stress dissipation
item.description: arXiv:2610.34498v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The data-to-solution map of the incompressible Euler equations is continuous but not uniformly continuous on Sobolev spaces, whereas viscosity makes the Navier--Stokes solution map Lipschitz continuous on small data, uniformly in time. This paper identifies the behavior of the solution map for a hybrid system sitting between these two extremes: the incompressible Oldroyd--B model in $\mathbb{R}^d$, $d=2,3$, in the high-Reynolds-number, high-Weissenberg-number regime. The velocity equation is a forced Euler equation and the only dissipation is a fractional diffusion $\eta(-\Delta)^\beta$, $\frac12\le\beta\le1$, acting on stress. We prove that, on the ball of small $H^s$ data ($s>1+\frac d2$) on which global solutions exist, the solution map is Lipschitz continuous with respect to the $H^{r}$-norm, $r=s-(2\beta-1)$, uniformly for all time, and Lipschitz into the natural dissipation spaces; the constant is explicit and tends to $\sqrt3$ as the size of the data tends to zero. Consequently the map is H\"older continuous into $C_b([0,\infty);H^{s'})$ for every $s'<s$, and is Lipschitz in $H^s$ itself when $\beta=\frac12$. Thus, although the velocity field is only transported, the solution map behaves like that of the Navier--Stokes equations rather than that of the Euler equations. The proof exploits the damped wave structure generated by the coupling between $u$ and $\nabla\cdot\tau$ through a Lyapunov functional with a cross term $(\delta u,\nabla\cdot\delta\tau)_{H^{r-\beta}}$, which transfers the stress dissipation to the velocity difference, together with a low-frequency interpolation argument that keeps all Gronwall coefficients integrable on $(0,\infty)$. The loss of $2\beta-1$ derivatives is exactly the gap between the hidden velocity dissipation of order $2(1-\beta)$ and the dissipation required by the Lipschitz estimate, and we show that it cannot be reduced by the energy method.
item.dc:creator: Gerard Misio{\l}ek, Jiahong Wu, Mingyu Yu

item.title: Mixing zone dynamics for the Saffman-Taylor instability with viscosity jump
item.description: arXiv:2610.34504v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct mixing solutions to the incompressible porous media equation for fully unstable Muskat initial data. The mixing zone expands linearly in time around an evolving central interface. Our approach combines the $h$-principle with the inversion of the associated Birkhoff-Rott operator, required when the viscosities differ. A key ingredient is to formulate this inversion in terms of the Saffman-Taylor function rather than the vorticity. This considerably simplifies the analysis and may be of independent interest for the Muskat problem.
item.dc:creator: Paula Luna-Velasco, Francisco Mengual

item.title: Lax Pair for the Kirchhoff-Pohozaev equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.34522v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the Kirchhoff-Pohozaev equation on any compact connected Riemannian manifold without boundary admits a Lax pair $(L,B)$, where $L$ is a self-adjoint finite-rank perturbation of the Laplace-Beltrami operator and $B$ is a skew-adjoint operator of finite rank, both depending analytically on the phase space variables. We study the spectrum of $L$ using the perturbative determinant which is known to determine its spectrum and to admit a product representation similar to that of the generating function in KdV. We use this to show that the dynamics of the integrals of motion constructed in \cite{BoitiManfrin2026,BHMP,campos} admits a Lax pair formulation with the same operator $L$ and to get a new proof of the involutivity of these integrals.
item.dc:creator: Dario Bambusi, Emanuele Haus, Simone Marrocco, Michela Procesi

item.title: Long-time action stability for perturbed KdV near finite-gap tori
item.description: arXiv:2610.34601v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove action and spectral stability near finite-gap tori of the periodic Korteweg--de Vries equation under autonomous analytic Hamiltonian perturbations of size $\varepsilon$. The estimates are uniform over prescribed compact families, without small-amplitude or nonresonance assumptions, and allow nearby initial data with infinitely many open gaps. Assuming a strong solution and a uniform higher Sobolev bound on $[0,T_0/\varepsilon]$, we permit one-derivative loss in the perturbing Hamiltonian's normal gradient. For sufficiently small $\varepsilon$ and initial normal Birkhoff size $r_0$, the tangential action variations and weighted sum of normal actions are bounded by $C_\delta(r_0^2+\varepsilon^{2\delta})$, while the spectral-gap variation in $\ell^2$ is bounded by $C_\delta(r_0+\varepsilon^\delta)$, for every $0<\delta<1/4$. A key ingredient is coercivity of the negative Hessian of the nonlinear KdV Hamiltonian on the full $\ell^2$ action space at every finite-gap action. We combine this with resonance analysis and corrected action observables evaluated along the solution. The hypotheses are verified for several local and nonlocal Hamiltonian perturbations.
item.dc:creator: Guan Huang

item.title: The Inhomogeneous Kinetic FPUT Equation near Rayleigh-Jeans Equilibria
item.description: arXiv:2610.34636v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the nonlinear dynamics of the spatially inhomogeneous kinetic wave equation associated with the FPUT-$\beta$ problem. We prove global-in-time well-posedness near nonsingular Rayleigh-Jeans equilibria and their asymptotic stability in particular in weighted $L^\infty$ norms in space and momentum, for small initial perturbations orthogonal to the collision kernel at almost every spatial point. We describe the spectrum near the origin at small spatial frequencies, identifying two simple eigenvalues with fractional and diffusive orders $|\xi|^{8/5}$ and $\xi^2$, respectively. Combining this spectral analysis with energy estimates taking into account the transport effect, we establish algebraic decay for the linear semigroup despite the absence of a spectral gap for the collision operator. We then use these estimates to obtain nonlinear stability.
item.dc:creator: Angeliki Menegaki, Haoling Xiang

item.title: A Deterministic Game-Theoretic Approach to Convexity-Preserving Property and Finite-Time Extinction of Level Sets for Geometric Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.34671v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the convexity-preserving property and finite-time extinction of level sets for quasilinear geometric equations using a game-theoretic approach introduced by Kohn and Serfaty. To construct the game whose value function approximates the viscosity solution, we use the approach introduced by Sato.
item.dc:creator: Yousuke Saga, Kazuhiro Takimoto

item.title: Unconditional uniqueness for the cubic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation in $H^{1/2}(\Bbb T^3)$
item.description: arXiv:2610.34733v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we establish unconditional uniqueness for the cubic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation (NLS) in the scaling-critical class $H^{1/2}(\mathbb{T}^3)$. Unlike approaches based on the GP-hierarchy or normal form reductions, which typically involve higher-order expansions, our proof works directly with the original cubic NLS, where we also make use of several new a priori Euclidean-like Strichartz estimates. More precisely, we show that every distributional solution in $C_tH_x^{1/2}$ belongs a priori to the class $L^2_{t,\mathrm{loc}}L_x^6$. The key ingredients are a suitable high-low modulation decomposition and the compactness of solution trajectories on bounded time intervals. We also exploit the preservation of the canonical symplectic form under the truncated NLS flow, in order to obtain necessary stability estimates in the rough Sobolev space $H^{-1/2}(\mathbb{T}^3)$.
item.dc:creator: Yongming Luo, Jiayu Zheng

item.title: Propagation dynamics of a parabolic-elliptic chemotaxis model in a time-periodic shifting environment
item.description: arXiv:2610.34753v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The current paper is devoted to the study of the propagation dynamics of a parabolic-elliptic chemotaxis model in a shifting environment. We investigate the scenario in which the favorable and unfavorable habitats are spatially separated, with the favorable habitat shifting at a time-periodic speed. We first establish the vanishing, persistence, and spreading properties of solutions with compactly supported and front-like initial data. In particular, we show that if the self-limitation rate of the species is large relative to the chemotactic sensitivity and the species is initially confined to a bounded region, then the species eventually becomes extinct when the habitat shifts rightward with a large average speed. In contrast, when the average shifting speed of the habitat is moderate, the species can persist and spread along the shifting habitat into an increasingly large spatial region. Finally, we establish the existence and nonexistence of time-periodic forced wave solutions whose wave speed coincides with the average shifting speed of the habitat.
item.dc:creator: Shuwen Xue, Xiao-Qiang Zhao

item.title: Liouville theorems for the stationary Navier-Stokes equations under partial component conditions
item.description: arXiv:2610.34780v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove Liouville theorems for smooth stationary incompressible Navier-Stokes flows in $R^3$ with finite Dirichlet integral and velocity vanishing uniformly at infinity. If the partial components of velocity $(u_1,u_2)$ belong to $L^{4,\infty}$, then we show that $u$ must vanish. The second result only requires that one component $u_1$ belongs to $L^{3/2,\infty}$. The proofs are based on the head-pressure sign and a localized energy identity, combined with different pressure estimates for the two cases.
item.dc:creator: Cuiyang Liu, Wei Luo

item.title: Designed short-time observations for rotational damping recovery in Timoshenko beams
item.description: arXiv:2610.34786v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the recovery of spatial rotational damping in a clamped Timoshenko beam. The coefficient belongs to a prescribed bounded finite-dimensional family. One fixed spatial average of rotation is recorded in separately labelled experiments with known initial rotational velocities. We construct these velocities so that the leading coefficient-to-data map is an invertible Gram matrix. Testing the equations against the smooth observation kernel gives a uniform parameter-Lipschitz remainder without differentiating the damping coefficient. A weighted temporal moment then yields global injectivity, Lipschitz stability and a globally convergent projected fixed-point reconstruction for sufficiently short observation times. Upper and deterministic two-point lower bounds give the same noise-amplification order $T^{-5/2}$ for $L^2$ time-history errors. A second sensitivity estimate supplies a separate sufficient condition for strong convexity and global projected-gradient convergence. We derive continuous and exact discrete adjoints, prove finite-time convergence of a conforming finite-element midpoint scheme, and propagate forward error into coefficient error. Reproducible synthetic experiments examine symmetry, gradient accuracy, noise and discretization bias.
item.dc:creator: Mohammad El-Hindi

item.title: Endpoint well-posedness for the Boussinesq equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.34793v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove small-data global well-posedness for the quadratic good Boussinesq equation on the real line and the circle at the endpoint $H^{-1/2}\times H^{-3/2}$. On each domain, a small invariant spectral set supports a continuous global group, with uniqueness in a fixed local integral class. In the periodic case, both components have zero mean and the flow is Lipschitz on bounded time intervals. The a priori bounds follow from a balanced perturbation determinant for the third-order Lax operator. Averaging two real spectral branches yields coercivity and frequency-tail control. On the line, we construct the endpoint flow by commuting Hamiltonians and Green-field estimates. On the circle, discrete spectral bounds and Kishimoto's endpoint local theory give global well-posedness.
item.dc:creator: Mingjuan Chen, Minjie Shan

item.title: Linear Stability, Inviscid Damping, and Scattering for Monotone Shear Flows in 2D Ideal MHD
item.description: arXiv:2610.34867v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the linearized 2D ideal incompressible magnetohydrodynamic equations around a monotone shear flow $(U(y),0)$ with a constant horizontal magnetic field $(\beta,0)$ on $\mathbb{T} \times \mathbb{R}$. For each fixed $\beta \neq 0$, we assume that the shear rate $U'$ is bounded above and below by positive constants and varies sufficiently slowly, although it need not be close to any constant. For every nontrivial perturbation with zero horizontal average, we establish sharp $L^2$ time rates in the corresponding paired norms: the horizontal velocity and magnetic components remain of order one, the vertical components decay at rate $\langle t \rangle^{-1}$, and the vorticity--current pair grows at rate $\langle t \rangle$. We prove strong $L^2$ scattering to two Alfv\'en profiles, identify the leading asymptotic behavior of the physical variables, and establish asymptotic completeness in the natural energy space.
item.dc:creator: Zhile Li

item.title: Effective Hamiltonians in Perforated Domains: Inf-Max formula and Stability
item.description: arXiv:2610.34910v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the dependence of the effective Hamiltonian $\overline H_\Omega(p)$ on the geometry of periodic perforated domains for convex Hamilton--Jacobi equations with state-constraint boundary conditions. We establish an inf--max representation over smooth test functions for domains with $C^1$ boundary. Using this representation, we derive a quantitative stability estimate in terms of the Hausdorff distance between domains and the reach of one boundary. This estimate yields convergence for non-nested domain approximations whose Hausdorff error is negligible relative to their boundary reach. Examples demonstrate the sharpness of the continuity modulus and show that Hausdorff convergence alone can fail to preserve the effective Hamiltonian, even for smooth domains and the quadratic Hamiltonian.
item.dc:creator: Yuxi Han, Son N. T. Tu

item.title: The Sharp Constant in the Second-Order Hydrogen Uncertainty Principle: Spectral Characterization and Quantitative Approximation
item.description: arXiv:2610.34916v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we study the sharp constant \(\mathcal H_d\) in the second-order Hydrogen Uncertainty Principle in every dimension \(d\ge2\). Using a spectral basis built from generalized Laguerre polynomials, together with a linearization procedure and spherical harmonic decomposition, we establish a spectral characterization of \(\mathcal H_d\). More precisely, we show that \[ \mathcal H_d = \frac12\min\{d+1,c_d^*\}, \] where \(c_d^*\in(0,d+3)\) is the unique parameter such that \[ \|S_{c_d^*}^{(d)}\|_{\ell^2\to\ell^2}=1. \] Here, for \(0<c<d+3\), \(S_c^{(d)}\) is an explicit positive Hilbert--Schmidt operator on \(\ell^2(\mathbb N_0)\). This characterization reveals a competition between the radial sector, which yields the value \(d+1\), and the first non-radial sector, encoded by the spectral parameter \(c_d^*\). For \(d\ge4\), we recover the known identity \[ \mathcal H_d=\frac{d+1}{2} \] through a spectral argument, giving an alternative proof of the results of Cazacu, Flynn and Lam \cite{CazacuFlynnLam} for \(d\ge5\) and Huang and Ye \cite{HuangYe} for \(d=4\). For \(d\in\{2,3\}\), this characterization yields \[ \mathcal H_d=\frac{c_d^*}{2}. \] We then exploit this spectral formulation to derive an explicit finite recursive scheme yielding effective two-sided bounds for \(\mathcal H_2\) and \(\mathcal H_3\), substantially improving the estimates of Huang and Ye \cite{HuangYe}.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed Jleli, Bessem Samet

item.title: Development of singular surfaces and formation of generic singularities in 3D pressureless flows
item.description: arXiv:2610.34958v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, the Cauchy problem for the equations of pressureless flows in three space dimensions is considered. It is well known that for smooth initial data, the density and velocity gradient often become unbounded at a finite time $t_0$. This type of singularity is associated with sticky-particle dynamics. For an open dense set of smooth initial data, the formation and structure of singularities are investigated using the transversality theorem, with the aid of constructive methods for initial velocity fields. In contrast to the two-dimensional case studied by Bressan, Chen and Huang (arXiv:2408.06877), for $t>t_0$ a singular hypersurface will be formed, whose governing system of equations is not hyperbolic. By assuming the initial data are analytic, we are able to precisely analyze the singular behavior of velocity and density. Based on this, the system of equations for singular hypersurfaces can be recast into a first-order system of Briot-Bouquet type, and the local analytic solution can be constructed using a version of the Cauchy-Kovalevskaya theorem.
item.dc:creator: Geng Chen, Faris El-Katri, Shoujun Huang

item.title: On Brezis' open problem 2.4
item.description: arXiv:2610.34979v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show the existence of a ``nonradial" smooth entire solution of the Ginzburg--Landau equation with degree $q\in\{8,9\}$ and modulus tending to one at infinity.
