This answers Brezis' Open Problem 2.4 negatively. To construct the counterexample, we vary a cone parameter $q \in [8, 9]$ and keeping the degree on the cone equal to one. Several key ingredients are needed. First, we need to compute the Morse index of radial vortex solutions at $q\in \{8, 9\}$. Second, we need to show compactness. Finally, Leray-Schauder degree theory and a homotopy argument yield the desired existence result.
item.dc:creator: Hong-Ge Chen, Yong Liu, Juncheng Wei, Wen Yang

item.title: Singular set estimates in quasilinear Alt-Caffarelli problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.34986v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a nonnegative, uniformly convex function $\Phi$, we study nonnegative minimizers of the quasilinear Alt-Caffarelli energy $\int_{\Omega}\Phi(\nabla u)+\chi_{\{u>0\}}$. Under mild regularity assumptions on $\Phi$, we show that the codimension of the singular set of the free boundary is at least $2+\eta$ for a positive $\eta$. With a singular minimizer in three dimensions in a forthcoming work, this result is sharp as long as integer dimensions are considered. Our proof method is flexible, and we use it to also prove a similar result for minimizers of the $p$-Laplacian counterpart of the Alt-Caffarelli energy.
item.dc:creator: Antonio De Rosa, Robin Neumayer, Hui Yu

item.title: Inverse heat source problem from terminal data on a set of low Hausdorff dimension
item.description: arXiv:2610.35014v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the recovery of a spatial source in the heat equation from terminal observations on a compact interior set $E$ with positive $\beta$ dimensional Hausdorff content for some $\beta>d-1$. The prescribed temporal forcing vanishes on a nontrivial interval immediately preceding the observation time. Under a spectral Sobolev prior and a quantitative noncancellation condition on the terminal spectral multipliers, we establish conditional logarithmic stability. For scattered observations on such sets, we derive a sampling inequality under a quasi uniformity assumption. Under explicit sampling and independent noise assumptions, we prove a logarithmic convergence rate in probability for the corresponding Tikhonov reconstructions with a data driven parameter choice. Two numerical experiments using a finite candidate approximation of a fixed Hausdorff set assess discrete spectral sampling stability and illustrate the effects of the waiting interval and measurement noise on reconstruction.
item.dc:creator: Kai Yu, Zhiyuan Li, Zhidong Zhang

item.title: Supercritical Geometric Optics for multidimensional scalar conservation laws
item.description: arXiv:2610.35034v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This article studies the propagation, near a smooth non-constant ground state, of monophase oscillatory wave trains with small amplitude and very high frequency for multidimensional nonlinear scalar conservation laws. These oscillations lie beyond the classical regime of uniformly bounded variation. Two scenarios may occur. Under suitable compatibility conditions, the oscillations propagate. Otherwise, they are damped through shock formation. In the baseline supercritical regime, we give an explicit criterion distinguishing these two behaviors and justify the corresponding asymptotic descriptions. At higher frequencies, the propagation mechanism becomes more restrictive and is governed by compatibility conditions involving a Lie algebra. Under a natural local constant-rank assumption, we obtain a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of complete WKB expansions. We also prove cancellation under first-order incompatibility. Perturbing a non-constant background state limits the propagation of small scales compared with the constant-background case. Our constructions contribute to the understanding of the fractional smoothing effect conjectured by Lions, Perthame and Tadmor.
item.dc:creator: Christophe Cheverry (IRMAR), Rida Harb (UniCA), St{\'e}phane Junca (LJAD)

item.title: Type-II Singularities of Immersed Locally Convex Curves Evolving under Generalized Anisotropic Gage Area-Preserving Flows with Slow Curvature Speeds
item.description: arXiv:2610.35064v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the singularity behavior of immersed locally convex closed plane curves evolving under generalized anisotropic Gage area-preserving flows with slow curvature speeds of the form $\kappa_\sigma^\alpha$, where $0<\alpha\le 1$. Here $\kappa_\sigma$ denotes the anisotropic curvature associated with a prescribed anisotropy function $\sigma$. We prove that every finite-time blow-up is of Type-II provided that the Euclidean length of the evolving curve remains uniformly bounded away from zero. This result holds without any symmetry assumptions on either the initial curve or the anisotropy. When the initial signed area is nonzero, this length lower bound is automatically satisfied, and thus any finite-time singularity is necessarily of Type-II. By means of Hamilton's rescaling method combined with a differential Harnack estimate, we show that along a suitable blow-up subsequence, the rescaled curves at the selected times converge locally to the profile of a translating solution of the corresponding anisotropic curvature flow $V=\kappa_\sigma^\alpha$. We also establish sufficient conditions for finite-time singularity formation in terms of the initial signed area and anisotropic length. Moreover, we construct locally convex initial curves arbitrarily close to the Wulff curve for which a finite-time Type-II singularity occurs.
item.dc:creator: Ze-Yu Ye, Xiao-Liu Wang

item.title: Smooth stationary water waves with multiple vortex spikes
item.description: arXiv:2610.35129v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For any prescribed positive integer $n$, we establish the existence of a family of stationary solutions to the two dimensional capillary-gravity water wave equations in finite depth, whose stream functions exhibit $n$ well-separated vertically aligned vortex spikes with alternating signs. The construction is based on a nonlinear gluing scheme for a singularly perturbed semilinear elliptic equation coupled to the Bernoulli equation on the free surface. Our results extend the single-spike construction to arbitrary finite multi-spike configurations and reveal a mechanism through which exponentially localized vortex spikes can coexist with an almost flat free surface.
item.dc:creator: Zhiqiang Fan, Yuchen Wang, Youquan Zheng

item.title: Non-local Interfacial Energies in Grain Boundaries via Dirichlet-to-Neumann Map and Energetic scaling
item.description: arXiv:2610.35133v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper deals with the variational analysis of edge dislocations arising in small-angle grain boundaries (Read--Shockley) and semi-coherent interfaces (van der Merwe). Using the Nabarro--Peierls approach to model edge dislocations, we reduce the two-dimensional isotropic Navier--Lam\'e system governing the linearized elastic energy to a one-dimensional non-local energy on the slip interface through a Dirichlet-to-Neumann map. We prove that the resulting boundary energy coincides, up to a multiplicative constant, with the fractional \(H^{\frac12}\)-Gagliardo seminorm of the displacement jump along the interface. Within this framework, we establish the existence of a unique global minimizer by combining our dimensional-reduction result with the characterization of De Luca, Goldman, and Ponsiglione. Indeed, we show that the optimal defect configuration is uniquely attained, up to translations, by an equispaced periodic array. Finally, we provide a physical rescaling that recovers the classical logarithmic energy regimes of both the Read--Shockley and van der Merwe models.
item.dc:creator: Valerio Corica, Francesco Santilli

item.title: Global regularity for a class of degenerate/singular Monge-Ampere equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.35192v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the global regularity of solutions to the homogeneous Dirichlet problem for a class of Monge-Ampere equations, which become degenerate or singular on the boundary due to the zero boundary value and the distance function. The degeneracy and singularity are described by the index - the sum of the powers of the distance function and the solution. We give a complete classification of the index, and prove that the solution is globally Holder continuous, log-Lipschitz continuous, $C^{1,eta}$, $C^{2,alpha}$ and $W^{2,p}$ respectively, depending on the size of the index. We also obtain estimates related to the five regularity results. All these results are optimal.
item.dc:creator: Fan Cui (School of Mathematics Science, Tianjin Normal University, Tianjin, China), Huaiyu Jian (School of Mathematics and Statistics, Beijing Technology and Business University, Beijing, China, Department of Mathematical Sciences, Tsinghua University, Beijing, China), You Li (School of Mathematics and Computational Science, Xiangtan University, Hunan, China), Yannan Liu (School of Mathematics and Statistics, Beijing Technology and Business University, Beijing, China)

item.title: Uniqueness and attractiveness of stationary solutions in a harvesting mean field game
item.description: arXiv:2610.35202v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sustainable harvesting of natural resources is a central challenge both in ecology and economics. This paper explores a MFG model for harvesting in an aquatic ecosystem. Such systems have recently attracted attention from the applied mathematics community, and, due to the interplay between the competition of agents and the internal dynamics of the fish population, the analytical properties of the resulting system are very delicate to study. In the present work, we focus on stationary solutions, with a strong emphasis on their uniqueness and dynamical stability.
item.dc:creator: Greta Lamonaca (IDP, CEREMADE, UO), Idriss Mazari (CEREMADE), Gr{\'e}goire Nadin (IDP, CNRS)

item.title: A PDE-Based Model of Runner Flow in Mass Participation Events
item.description: arXiv:2610.35206v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a macroscopic approach for modeling pedestrian movement. A convection-diffusion partial differential equation (PDE) is described and used to model the flow of runners along a marathon course. A marathon is a good modeling case study for human movement because the location of runners is only known in sparse locations, so an accurate model is needed to know where people are at all times. As well, marathons offer many safety and logistical problems that can be solved by modeling human movement. Data is obtained from the 2023 Columbus Marathon, and model improvements are made to include a temporally varying convection term. Results show an increase in model accuracy which can allow for better resource allocation and safety measures.
item.dc:creator: Alice Molinari, Brian Block, Stephanie Stockar, Simona Sacone

item.title: On the symmetric Morrey problem in three dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.35216v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the relations between seven generalized notions of convexity for continuous integrands in the space of symmetric $3\times 3$ matrices. Here, symmetric quasiconvexity is defined through symmetrized gradients, and symmetric rank-one convexity through symmetrized rank-one lines. We construct a symmetric quasiconvex integrand that is not polyconvex at symmetric matrices, and an integrand that is both symmetric rank-one convex and Hessian quasiconvex but not symmetric quasiconvex. We also establish a transfer principle that converts smooth rank-one convex functions that lack Hessian quasiconvexity into symmetric rank-one convex integrands while preserving this lack of of Hessian quasiconvexity. Applying this scheme to already existing counterexamples yields the existence of symmetric rank-one convex integrands that are not Hessian quasiconvex. Together with known examples, these results determine all pairwise implications among the seven notions considered here.
item.dc:creator: Florian Gammer

item.title: Liouville Theorems for the Stationary Fractional Hall-Magnetohydrodynamic Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.35260v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we prove Liouville-type theorems for the stationary fractional Hall-magnetohydrodynamic equations in $\mathbb R^3$. Smooth solutions vanishing at infinity, with $u\in\dot H^{\alpha/2}$ and $b\in\dot H^{\beta/2}$, are trivial for $1\le\alpha\le\frac53$, $1\le\beta<2$ and $\alpha+2\beta\le5$, with no additional integrability assumption. The key step is to estimate the Hall boundary term through the Caffarelli--Silvestre extension of $b$.
item.dc:creator: Albert Ai, Gaston Vergara-Hermosilla

item.title: Regularization and Full Support for the CBO Equation with Measure Initial Data
item.description: arXiv:2610.35266v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove global well-posedness and regularization for the isotropic consensus-based optimization equation with initial probability measures of finite fourth moment. Under suitable weight decay assumptions, after any nonconstant consensus motion, both the density and the consensus trajectory become smooth, and all spatial Sobolev norms are locally bounded in time. The proof uses a Fourier commutator estimate, localization and iteration, followed by a nonlinear time bootstrap. Counterexamples show that smoothing can fail at a stationary consensus point. For non-Dirac initial data, we also prove positivity away from the consensus point and full support at every positive time in all dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Lukang Sun

item.title: A theoretically exact filtered back-propagationformula for single-time wave inversion
item.description: arXiv:2610.35302v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider single-time wave inversion, that is, recovering the initial pressure $f$ from the wave field $\mathcal{W}_T f = u(\cdot,T)$ at a single time $T$, where $u$ solves the wave equation with sound speed $c$ and initial data $(f,0)$. In two dimensions this is the main reconstruction step of full-field photoacoustic projection imaging, where each camera image is a two-dimensional wave field at a single time instant. An efficient direct method is back-propagation by the Fourier multiplier $2\cos(cT|\xi|)$. It yields exact inversion in odd dimensions but not in two. We give its error in closed form, with bounds, and derive an exact explicit filtered back-propagation $f = 2\mathcal{W}_T \mathcal{M}_K \mathcal{W}_T f$ in analogy to filtered backprojection for the Radon transform.
item.dc:creator: Markus Haltmeier

item.title: Quantitative Analysis of Second-Harmonic Generation in Plasmonic Nanowires: Symmetry Breaking and a Topological Defect
item.description: arXiv:2610.35307v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper develops a quantitative theory of second-harmonic generation (SHG) in hollow plasmonic nanowires, distinguishing geometric symmetry breaking from cavity effects. We consider a centrosymmetric material with a concentric circular cavity and a slightly perturbed outer boundary. Relative to the solid nanowire in~\cite{liu2026quantitative}, the cavity introduces a topological defect by changing the cross-section from a disk to a doubly connected domain, whereas the outer-boundary perturbation breaks geometric symmetry. Local inversion-symmetry breaking at the interfaces induces nonlinear surface polarization. Using layer potentials and boundary-perturbation asymptotics, we derive explicit leading- and first-order formulas for the fundamental and second-harmonic fields. For a circular outer boundary, the leading-order second-harmonic field is purely quadrupolar; its amplitude differs from the solid-wire case by $O(\gamma^2)$ as $\gamma=r_i/r_e\to0$ and decays as $O(r_e-r_i)$ in the nonresonant thin-shell limit. For perturbations proportional to $\cos(n\theta)$, $n\ge3$, the first-order second-harmonic correction contains only modes $n-2$, $n$, and $n+2$, yielding dipolar, quadrupolar, or higher-order radiation for $n=3$, $n=4$, or $n\ge5$, respectively, provided the lowest-order modal coefficient is nonzero. We derive plasmonic resonance conditions at both frequencies and estimate the singular orders of single and simultaneous resonances, including possible higher-order singularities from coincident resonance factors. Thus geometric symmetry determines the multipolar modes, whereas the cavity radius controls their amplitudes and resonant enhancement.
item.dc:creator: Qi Lei, Hongyu Liu, Zhi-Qiang Miao, Guang-Hui Zheng

item.title: Uniform Exponential Stability for Finite Energy Weak Solutions to the Barotropic Compressible Navier--Stokes Equations with Large Potential External Forces
item.description: arXiv:2610.35320v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the large-time behavior of Lions--Feireisl finite energy weak solutions to the barotropic compressible Navier--Stokes equations in three-dimensional bounded domains with Dirichlet boundary conditions and large potential external forces. For $\gamma>3/2$, we prove that these weak solutions converge exponentially to the steady state as time tends to infinity, provided that the steady density is bounded away from zero. The main novelty of our analysis is a compactness argument based on Young measures. Furthermore, we prove that the Young measures generated by the density are Dirac measures. Together with the extra integrability of the density, this yields strong convergence to the nonconstant steady density and uniform smallness of the energy $w$ for sufficiently large time. We use Taylor expansion and the Bogovskii operator to construct a Lyapunov functional, and use this smallness of $w$ to obtain exponential decay with a time $T_0$, which is independent of the particular weak solution, thereby answering the question raised by Kang, Peng and Xiong in \cite[Remark~1.1]{KPX}. Corresponding decay estimates for the density, momentum, kinetic energy and the viscous dissipation integrated from large times to infinity also hold, allowing vacuum.
item.dc:creator: Xin Song, Chengfeng Xiong

item.title: Ground states for Brezis-Nirenberg-type fractional elliptic systems with sublinear absorption and subcritical perturbation
item.description: arXiv:2610.35365v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper addresses the non-local fractional counterpart of the Laplace equation involving critical nonlinearities, a famous problem originally investigated by Brezis and Nirenberg in [Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 36(4) (1983), pp. 437--477]. We study a class of fractional elliptic systems and equations with critical exponents, sublinear absorption, subcritical perturbation, and general noncoercive frequency parameters. The work is carried out both within a general framework involving non-local integrodifferential operators and in specific concrete models. Our results extend and complement the existing literature on critical fractional elliptic problems in several directions: (1) we include sublinear absorption together with a subcritical perturbation, so that the overall nonlinearity is not superlinear at zero; (2) we provide two types of concrete verification of the energy threshold condition in the presence of the critical term, the sublinear absorption, and the subcritical perturbation, whereas the existing verifications are restricted to the pure critical case; (3) we obtain ground state solutions for coupled systems, not merely nontrivial solutions for scalar equations; (4) we allow a general noncoercive range of frequency parameters, including negative values.
item.dc:creator: Guanwei Chen

item.title: The metastability phenomen for a radiative gas model
item.description: arXiv:2610.35387v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the time-asymptotic behaviour of solutions to a singular perturbation of the inviscid Burgers problem describing sound propagation in a radiating gas. This radiating gas model exhibits the interesting phenomenon known as metastability that has been first identified for the viscous Burgers equation. Precisely, on an initial time span, that scales linearly in the inverse of the perturbation parameter, we can quantify the L1-distance of the solution to the so-called sharp N-wave solution of the inviscid Burgers problem and to a diffusive N-wave. On a second long-time stage that scales exponentially in the inverse of the perturbation parameter, the solutions still remain close to a diffusive N-wave before finally collapsing into diffusion waves. Besides our analysis of the radiating gas model, we also provide an alternative description of metastability in the viscous Burgers model which, unlike other studies, relies on L1-estimates and does not require the passage to similarity variables.
item.dc:creator: Christian Rohde, Adrian Viorel

item.title: Periodic dynamics of transonic shocks in Euler-Poisson flows
item.description: arXiv:2610.35402v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies the existence and dynamical stability of time-periodic transonic shock solutions to the one-dimensional Euler--Poisson equations under periodic boundary perturbations. The analysis relies on two key mechanisms: the structural dissipation induced by the transonic shock and the stabilization effect of the positive electric field on the shock position. Using a reformulation of the Rankine-Hugoniot conditions and uniform estimates on the flow and shock perturbations, we establish the existence of a time-periodic transonic shock solution. We further prove its dynamical stability under small perturbations of the initial data.
item.dc:creator: Peng Qu, Jiahui Wang

item.title: Quantitative approximation theorem of neural operators for the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map
item.description: arXiv:2610.35404v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study neural operators for the Dirichet-to-Neumann map (DN map), which is encountered in the famous Calder\'on's problem. In many numerical methods used for reconstructing the unknown conductivity from the knowledge of the DN map need to evaluate the corresponding DN map at a given conductivity function, which involves solving the boundary value problem for the conductivity equation and taking the Neumann data. Such procedure is time consuming and not effective. Hence, it is a favorable strategy to construct a surrogate to replace the forward map mapping conductivity functions to corresponding DN maps. The main theme of this paper is to derive quantitative bounds on the parametric complexity of these neural operators. In particular, under suitable assumptions, their depth grows at most logarithmically with $\varepsilon^{-1}$, while the relevant spectral and projection ranks grow algebraically. It should be noted that general neural operators suffer from "the curse of parametric dimensionality". This work demonstrates the construction of neural operators for the DN map that does not suffer from such curse.
item.dc:creator: Pu-Yun Kow, Andrea Aspri, Elisa Francini, Jenn-Nan Wang

item.title: Gevrey Regularity for a Sum of Two Squares in Two Variables
item.description: arXiv:2610.35427v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Gevrey hypoellipticity of a sum of two squares in two variables, satisfying the H\"ormander hypothesis, assuming that the function, $ q $, describing (the space projection of) its characteristic variety vanishes only at a single point, which can be assumed to be the origin. A hypoellipticity result is given in a Gevrey class, depending on $ q $. In some examples the found regularity is known to be optimal.
item.dc:creator: Antonio Bove, Marco Mughetti

item.title: Log-Concavity and Fundamental Gaps on Complex Projective Domains
item.description: arXiv:2610.35431v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove quantitative log-concavity and fundamental-gap estimates for Dirichlet Schr\"odinger operators on complex projective domains. With holomorphic sectional curvature four, the boundary condition $\mathrm{II}\ge\sqrt{44/5}\,g$ suffices in every complex dimension under $\operatorname{Hess} V\ge2|\nabla V|g$ and $\operatorname{osc}V\le4n$. It yields $\operatorname{Hess}(-\log\phi_1)>g$ and $\lambda_2-\lambda_1>\max\{n+2+\sqrt{n^2+5n+11},\,2n+14/3\}$. The main difficulty is to control the distinguished Hopf direction together with a transverse Hessian block whose dimension grows with $n$. We extend modified-Hessian first-contact arguments by retaining the Hopf term and using longitudinal and transverse rotational tests. A trace minimization reduces all gradient orientations to three extreme directions. A dimension-scaled logarithmic barrier then compares their contact costs with a single limiting profile. A radial spectral estimate supplies the required quadratic-in-dimension spectral threshold from a dimension-independent boundary curvature bound. For $n\ge3$ these are, to our knowledge, the first log-concavity estimates for domains in $\mathbb{CP}^n$ without symmetry assumptions. We also prove a sharp diameter bound and Hessian levels linear in $n$ under larger dimension-free curvature bounds.
item.dc:creator: Gunhee Cho

item.title: The role of density in phase transitions and new perspectives on theta functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.35437v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $z\in \mathbb{H}:=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:\Im(z)>0\}$ and $\Lambda:=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\Im(z)}}\big({\mathbb Z}\oplus z{\mathbb Z}\big)$, and set $ \theta(\alpha;z):=\theta(\alpha;\Lambda)=\sum_{(m,n)\in\mathbb{Z}^2}e^{-\pi\alpha \frac{|m+nz|^2}{\Im(z)}}. $ We study the minimization of the functional $\theta(\alpha;z)-b\theta(2\alpha;z)$ and establish a complete phase diagram for all $\alpha>0$ and $b\in(0,\sqrt{2})$. For $0<b<\sqrt{2}$, an explicit threshold $b_1=0.0767767081\cdots\in(0,1/10)$ separates two distinct types of phase transitions. Type I: $0<b<b_1$: it admits a type of ``hexagonal--rhombic--square--rectangular'' phase transition. Type II: $b_1\le b<\sqrt{2}$: it admits a type of ``hexagonal--square--rectangular'' phase transition, without passing through the rhombic lattices. These phase transitions contrast with Montgomery's theorem \cite{Mon1988}, where the hexagonal lattice minimizes the single theta function at all scales, and the recent B\'{e}termin-Faulhuber-Steinerberger theorem \cite{BFS2026} for translated Gaussian lattice sums, where the hexagonal lattice prevails in a min-max structure. In our setting, the density parameter $\alpha$ governs the sequence of optimal lattice shapes, while the competition parameter $b$ controls the emergence of the rhombic phase, which exists for $b<b_1$ and vanishes for $b\ge b_1$. As an application, we resolve B\'etermin's conjecture \cite{Betermin2021AHP}. B\'etermin predicted a Type I phase transition for the functional $\theta(\alpha;z)-(1/10)\theta(2\alpha;z)$ with $b=1/10$. We instead rigorously establish that no rhombic lattice is a global minimizer at any density and prove that the system undergoes a Type II phase transition, thereby settling the conjecture in corrected form.
item.dc:creator: Kaixin Deng, Senping Luo

item.title: Boundary Layer Criterion for the Low Mach Number and Inviscid Limits in Compressible Fluid-Rigid Body Interaction
item.description: arXiv:2610.35441v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the simultaneous low Mach number and vanishing viscosity limit for a three-dimensional compressible viscous fluid interacting with a freely moving rigid body. The fluid satisfies the compressible Navier-Stokes equations and the no-slip condition on the body surface, while the body evolves according to Newton's laws driven by the fluid stresses. We establish convergence of finite-energy weak solutions to a strong solution of the corresponding incompressible Euler-rigid body system on its interval of existence. Assuming that the initial relative energy tends to zero, convergence holds under a Kato-type condition in a boundary layer whose thickness is proportional to the viscosity. This condition combines vanishing viscous dissipation with a weighted estimate on the fluid momentum relative to the rigid body motion. The proof uses the relative entropy method and a boundary layer corrector adapted to the fluid-rigid body coupling, providing a sufficient condition for convergence in relative energy as the Mach number and viscosity tend to zero simultaneously.
item.dc:creator: Kuntal Bhandari, \v{S}\'{a}rka Ne\v{c}asov\'{a}, Arnab Roy

item.title: The divergence of continuously differentiable vector fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.35452v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For $m\geq 2$, we give a complete characterisation of the continuous functions on $\mathbb{R}^m$ that are divergences of continuously differentiable vector fields. The characterisation is formulated in terms of distributions and, equivalently, in terms of the continuous dual of a suitably topologised subspace of the Arens--Eells space. The two implications yield contrasting applications. First, there exists a compactly supported continuous function which is the divergence of a bounded Lipschitz vector field but not of any continuously differentiable vector field. Second, every continuous function whose distributional partial derivatives are locally $m$-integrable (the critical exponent for Sobolev embedding) is the divergence of a continuously differentiable vector field.
item.dc:creator: Thierry De Pauw

item.title: Extremal Trudinger-Moser inequality associated with many point vortices with multi-intensities
item.description: arXiv:2610.35471v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the boundedness of extremal 2D Trudinger-Moser inequality associated with many point vortices with multi-intensities. Sufficient conditions for continuously-distributed measures are given in one-sided and two-sided cases.
item.dc:creator: Takashi Suzuki, Yohei Toyota

item.title: Differentiability and Convexity of the Solution Maps for Fully Non-linear Parabolic HJB Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.35476v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the dependence on the terminal condition of solutions to a fully nonlinear parabolic Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman (HJB) equation, when the terminal condition varies along a finite-dimensional family. This problem is motivated by a dual formulation of semimartingale optimal transport. The equation is posed as a terminal-value Cauchy problem on an unbounded spatial domain. Under structural ellipticity and regularity assumptions on the nonlinear operator, we recall local parabolic H\"older estimates and stability results for bounded uniformly continuous terminal data. We then establish continuous directional differentiability of the solution map with respect to the finite-dimensional parameter, and identify its derivative through the corresponding linearized Cauchy problem. Under an additional convexity assumption on the Hamiltonian and a non-degeneracy condition on the terminal data, we prove local strong convexity of the point-evaluated solution map. The analysis relies on Evans--Krylov theory for fully nonlinear parabolic equations and combines PDE arguments with probabilistic representations. Finally, we extend the differentiability and convexity results to cascades of Cauchy problems in which successive equations are coupled through terminal conditions at several prescribed times. This structure is motivated, for instance, by optimal transport problems with marginal constraints imposed at several maturities.
item.dc:creator: Jean-Fran\c{c}ois Chassagneux, St\'ephane Cr\'epey, Gr\'egoire Loeper, Justin Ruelland

item.title: A Liouville Theorem for the Real k-Hessian Equation with a One-Sided Growth Condition
item.description: arXiv:2610.35565v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a scale-invariant interior $C^2$ estimate for smooth solutions of the real $k$-Hessian equation. As an application, we prove that every smooth entire solution of $\sigma_k(D^2u)=1$ satisfying $u(x)\ge b|x|^2-B$ for some constants $b,B$ with $b>0$ is a quadratic polynomial. For smooth solutions, admissibility is forced by the growth condition. The results also hold for viscosity solutions and for weak solutions in Trudinger's sense. Admissibility is required in the latter case.
item.dc:creator: Jingchen Hu, Heming Jiao

item.title: Gradient estimates and Liouville theorems for exponentially harmonic functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.35571v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study exponentially harmonic functions on complete Riemannian manifolds. Under a lower Ricci curvature bound \(\Ric_g\geq-Kg\), we first establish a local gradient estimate in terms of the oscillation. We then prove a pointwise gradient estimate for solutions bounded from one side. As an application, when \(\Ric_g\geq0\), we obtain a Liouville theorem under a one-sided sublinear growth condition. In particular, every exponentially harmonic function bounded above or below is constant.
item.dc:creator: Xishen Jin, Xi Zhang

item.title: Asymptotic observable symmetry for spacetime observability of waves II: Smooth bounded domains
item.description: arXiv:2610.35610v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Continuing \cite{NWX} and Part I \cite{AOSI}, we further investigate symmetry for spacetime observability of wave equations. Building on asymptotic observable symmetry (AOS) introduced in \cite{AOSI}, we study symmetry under glancing propagation and caustics. We prove that, on every smooth bounded domain in $\R^2$ and for every positive observation time, there is a fixed measurable set satisfying the essential spacetime measurable geometric control condition. However, the observability inequality fails on this set.
item.dc:creator: Jingrui Niu, Shengquan Xiang

item.title: Sharp volume tests and entropy thresholds for quasilinear elliptic inequalities with gradient reactions
item.description: arXiv:2610.35688v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate positive weak solutions of $-\Delta_m u\ge u^p|\nabla u|^q$ on complete noncompact Riemannian manifolds without curvature, volume doubling, or Poincar\'e assumptions. For the superhomogeneous mixed reaction we derive a curvature-free integral volume test by combining two first-order estimates with a recurrence for the mass of a \emph{fixed} density. The same approach organizes the pure-gradient and capacity criteria and yields sharp finite hierarchies of iterated-logarithmic growth bounds, with counterexamples on smooth model manifolds. In the subhomogeneous region, vanishing lower growth of $\log V(R)/R^{m-q}$ forces the Liouville property. On the homogeneous line $p+q=m-1$, we obtain the optimal strict lower-volume-entropy threshold $(p+1)((m-1)/p)^{p/(p+1)}$ for $p>0$ (and $1$ for $p=0$), together with examples at equality. The existing six-region classification is not claimed as new; the advances concern refined volume hypotheses and their model sharpness. The tests remain valid for smooth weighted measures and for locally bounded positive Sobolev solutions. Sharpness is understood within the stated model families; no characterization from volume alone on an individual manifold is asserted.
item.dc:creator: Yongheng Qin, Yuhua Sun, Jie Xiao

item.title: Unconditional scattering below the ground state for the three-dimensional focusing energy-critical generalized Hartree equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.35700v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Unconditional global existence and scattering are established for the three-dimensional focusing energy-critical generalized Hartree equation with $0<\alpha<3$, below the ground-state energy and kinetic thresholds. The initial data lie in $\dot H^1$, with no radial symmetry, finite-mass, or finite-variance assumption. Annular frequency estimates and Gaussian interaction estimates rule out a compact critical trajectory by first controlling its nonlinear forcing and then recovering its conserved mass.
item.dc:creator: Pang-hung Chung, Dan Han

item.title: Existence and uniqueness of solutions for a random PDE-ODE model describing glioma invasion and radiotherapy
item.description: arXiv:2610.35763v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a stochastic model for the growth and invasion of glioma cells in the anisotropic brain tissue, also incorporating effects of radiotherapeutic interventions and associated uncertainties. The PDE-ODE model couples glioma and healthy tissue dynamics in a nonlinear manner and explicitly includes treatment-related stochasticity through random depletion terms. The macroscopic system has been obtained by an upscaling procedure from a microscopic description in [1]. We prove the existence and uniqueness of local strong solutions to the corresponding stochastic system. The analysis addresses challenges arising from the nonlinear coupling, anisotropic diffusion, taxis mechanisms, and stochastic treatment effects, providing a first rigorous step toward the mathematical understanding of stochastic continuum models for glioma invasion and therapy response.
item.dc:creator: Martina Conte, Sandesh Athni Hiremath, Christina Surulescu

item.title: Traveling Waves for Mixed Nonlocal-Local Systems of Conservation Laws on $\mathbb{S}^1$
item.description: arXiv:2610.35771v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Non trivial traveling waves in genuinely nonlinear conservation laws hardly appear and, in some cases, scalar nonlocal conservation laws inherit this feature. Here, we show that mixed nonlocal-local systems of conservation laws display a far richer scenario. A variety of traveling waves may exist, different components may travel with different speeds and traveling waves can appear as time-asymptotic limits. Technically, these results need a significant extension of Dafermos' "trend to steady state" theory, exploiting properties of Hamiltonian systems solved by generalized characteristics.
item.dc:creator: Rinaldo M. Colombo, Mauro Garavello, Claudia Nocita

item.title: On the Nash equilibrium for a model of traffic flow
item.description: arXiv:2610.35772v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The paper consider a conservation law model of traffic flow on a highway, where each driver chooses an optimal departure time $\tau^d$, based on a departure cost $\varphi(\tau^d)$ and an arrival cost $\psi(\tau^a)$. Nash equilibria are studied, where no driver can reduce his own cost by changing his departure time. The first results provide continuity estimates on the arrival time, depending on the distribution of departures. In terms of the ${\bf L}^1$ distance, we show that the corresponding map is H\"older continuous with exponent $1/2$ in Lagrangian variables (labelling individual drivers), and Lipschitz continuous in Eulerian space variables. Concerning the regularity of the a Nash equilibrium, our results show that, when the total number of drivers is sufficiently large, a queue alway forms at the entrance of the highway and the corresponding traffic density contains a shock. Moreover, for any number of drivers (possibly small), we prove that for generic $\mathcal C^2$ cost functions $\varphi, \psi$ the Nash equilibrium solution still contains a shock. In the last section of the paper, assuming that the initial departure rate is not a Nash equilibrium, we consider an evolution equation for the departure rate, where each driver keeps changing his daily departure time in order to reduce his own cost. It is proved that this nonlocal integro-differential evolution equation admits a unique solution, globally in time. This provides some theoretical support to earlier numerical simulations, which indicated the dynamic instability of the Nash equilibrium and the possible existence of a chaotic attractor.
item.dc:creator: Alberto Bressan, Daniel Lee Harmon, Elio Marconi

item.title: The generic structure of the singular set in the Stefan problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.35780v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that, in every space dimension $n\ge2$, the singular set $\Sigma$ of a generic (in the Baire-category sense) solution of the Stefan problem is countably parabolically $(n-2)$-rectifiable. In particular, $\dim_{\mathrm{par}}(\Sigma)\le n-2$. This is achieved by proving the following sharp result: in every space dimension, points of the maximal stratum of a generic solution are discrete in space-time.
item.dc:creator: Giacomo Colombo, Alessio Figalli

item.title: Parabolic Rectifiable Reifenberg for Measures
item.description: arXiv:2610.35809v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We announce a structure theory for measures on $\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}$ equipped with the parabolic distance. Our results include a parabolic rectifiable Reifenberg theorem for arbitrary Radon measures, qualitative and quantitative characterizations of regular parabolic rectifiability by Jones square functions, and sharp results for $L^p$ beta numbers. The results hold in every parabolic dimension and extend the theories of Edelen--Naber--Valtorta, Azzam--Tolsa and David--Semmes to space-time. The stated theorems and corollaries, together with their proofs, are formalized in Lean~4 with Mathlib.
item.dc:creator: Robert Koirala

item.title: Characteristic gluing to extremal Kerr horizons and the third law of black hole thermodynamics in vacuum
item.description: arXiv:2610.35836v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a non-perturbative, non-axisymmetric characteristic gluing theorem for the Einstein vacuum equations: every Boyer-Lindquist sphere in the domain of outer communication of a Kerr black hole, in particular every symmetry sphere of a Schwarzschild exterior, can be glued along a single outgoing null hypersurface to a horizon sphere of an extremal Kerr black hole of sufficiently large mass. The gluing is exact at both ends and matches the full sphere data, including the transversal curvature. This proves a conjecture of Kehle and Unger in the extremal case. We first raise the angular momentum to the extremal value by rotating shear pulses of non-axisymmetric gravitational radiation, and then damp the incoming data exponentially along a long non-expanding neck. At the degenerate target horizon we invert the linearised problem at all angular frequencies, using a factorisation of a fourth-order angular operator into an angular Teukolsky-Starobinsky product. As an application, we construct one-ended asymptotically flat vacuum initial data whose maximal development contains an exactly Schwarzschild apparent horizon and, at a later advanced time, an exactly extremal Kerr event horizon. This is the first rigorous counterexample to the third law of black hole thermodynamics in vacuum, and proves a second conjecture of Kehle and Unger.
item.dc:creator: Stefan Czimek

item.title: $C^{1,\alpha}$ and $W^{2,1+\varepsilon}$ regularity for the $2$-Hessian equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.35839v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, for every $\varepsilon>0$, we establish interior and global a priori $C^{1,\alpha}$ estimates for some $\alpha\in(0,1)$ from $W^{2,1+\varepsilon}$ bounds for bounded smooth $2$-admissible solutions of the $2$-Hessian equation, with the interior estimate requiring only an upper bound on the density. Under positive upper and lower density bounds, we prove global $W^{2,1+\varepsilon}$ estimates for some $\varepsilon>0$ on bounded strictly mean convex $C^{2,\beta}$ domains with $C^{2,\beta}$ boundary values. For densities bounded above and below by positive constants, the interior $C^{1,\alpha}$ estimate follows by combining the first result with an interior $W^{2,1+\varepsilon}$ estimate obtained by a slight modification of an existing argument. Combining the first result with the global $W^{2,1+\varepsilon}$ estimate yields the global $C^{1,\alpha}$ estimate. Known examples show that the $C^{2,\beta}$ regularity assumptions on the boundary and boundary values are optimal in the H\"older scale for both the global $W^{2,1+\varepsilon}$ estimate and the global $C^{1,\alpha}$ estimate.
item.dc:creator: Yasheng Lyu

item.title: Optimal Non-Homogeneous Improvements of the Anisotropic Hardy Inequality
item.description: arXiv:2610.33346v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the Hardy inequality associated with a strongly convex Finsler norm $F$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ and we study its optimal non-homogeneous improvements in the whole range $1<p<\infty$. We show that the anisotropic Hardy difference controls a weighted critical Sobolev norm when $1<p<n$, a weighted exponential integrability of Trudinger type when $p=n$, where the Hardy term is replaced by its Leray logarithmic correction, and a weighted H\"older seminorm when $p>n$, proving in each regime that the logarithmic weights appear with the optimal exponents. In the borderline case $p=n$ this extends to general functions the optimal exponent previously known only for anisotropically radial functions. The proofs rely on a common ground-state reduction, combined with a splitting into an $F_o$-radial and a mean-free part for $1<p\le n$, and with an anisotropic Morrey representation formula for $p>n$.
item.dc:creator: Giuseppina di Blasio, Giovanni Pisante, Georgios Psaradakis

item.title: Price's law for scalar waves on 1+4 dimensional subextremal Myers-Perry spacetimes
item.description: arXiv:2610.33812v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider Myers--Perry spacetimes $(M,g_{\mathbf{a},\mathbf{b},\mathfrak{m}})$ in $1+4$ dimensions with two spin parameters $(\mathbf{a},\mathbf{b})\in\mathbb{R}^2$, which are a direct generalization of the well known Kerr spacetime in $1+3$ dimensions. We prove that the Hamiltonian flow associated to $g_{\mathbf{a},\mathbf{b},\mathfrak{m}}^{-1}$ is normally hyperbolically trapped for the full subextremal range \[ (|\mathbf{a}|+|\mathbf{b}|)^2<2\mathfrak{m}. \] As an application, we prove a Price law with explicit leading order terms for solutions $\phi(t,x)$ of the scalar wave equation \[ \Box_{g_{\mathbf{a},\mathbf{b},\mathfrak{m}}}\phi=0 \] under the assumption of real mode stability. Our precise asymptotics imply that $\phi(t,x)=ct^{-3}+\mathcal{O}(t^{-4+})$, where $c\in\mathbb{C}$ is an explicitly computable constant.
item.dc:creator: Pieter-Bart Peters

item.title: Gravitational Radiation Coupled to a real massive scalar Field
item.description: arXiv:2610.33928v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the asymptotic behavior of small-data global solutions to the Einstein--Klein--Gordon system with a positive-mass real scalar field in wave gauge. We show that the linearized trace component of the metric perturbation admits a $\hat t^{-1}\simeq t^{-1}$ optimal decreasing rate. Moreover, a quantitative one-point observability estimate is established: the initial Klein-Gordon energy is controlled by this leading order coefficient.
item.dc:creator: Yue Ma, Xianghao Wu, Weidong Zhang

item.title: Integrable distortion II: the p-Weil-Petersson variational problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.34007v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the hyperbolically weighted distortion energies \[ \mathcal{I}_p(f)=\int_\mathbb{D} \frac{|\mu_f|^p}{(1-|\mu_f|^2)^{\max\{2,p\}/2}}\,dA_\eta \] for finite-distortion disk homeomorphisms with prescribed boundary values, together with the associated inverse problem in the monotone Sobolev class. For $1<p\leq2$, the inverse density is polyconvex precisely when $p\geq p_{\mathrm c}=1+1/\sqrt2$. In this range, quasisymmetric data with finite-energy monotone barriers yield minimisers with holomorphic Ahlfors--Hopf differentials and strong local Sobolev convergence of minimising subsequences. For $p_{\mathrm c}<p<2$, a finite-energy finite-distortion barrier yields a unique absolute monotone minimiser, which is a quasiconformal diffeomorphism and is asymptotically conformal. Together with the boundary-class theorem of Part~I, this characterises the admissible boundary data as $T^p$. The proof combines a selected barrier approximation, uniform scalar gradient estimates and a weighted Reich--Strebel comparison. For $1<p<p_{\mathrm c}$, finite rank-one comparisons bound distortion on the positive-Jacobian set by a cutoff strictly below the ellipticity cutoff. An attained monotone minimum is either a quasiconformal diffeomorphism or has nonzero rank-one derivatives on a set of positive area. For $0<p\leq1$, minimisers with finite distortion, or homeomorphic minimisers with a locally Sobolev inverse, are M\"obius maps. We also obtain energy-dependent quasiconformal bounds for regular minimisers when $p>2$. \
item.dc:creator: Gaven Martin, Cong Yao

item.title: Sharp gradient comparison and rigidity for semilinear equations on manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.34207v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove sharp amplitude and gradient comparisons for positive solutions of a class of semilinear elliptic equations on complete manifolds under a Ricci lower bound. Equality at one point characterizes hyperbolic space and the corresponding radial solution. The local estimates are uniform in the mixing coefficients and number of terms for positive mixtures of subcritical powers. For a class of conformal compactifications defined by a source equation, we obtain sharp boundary scalar-curvature bounds and hyperbolic rigidity. We also construct non-Einstein examples whose normalization persists under small compactly supported metric perturbations.
item.dc:creator: Linlin Sun

item.title: Length bounds and rigidity for ancient curve shortening flow on warped product surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.34274v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study ancient solutions to curve shortening flow on a class of warped product surfaces. For closed embedded ancient solutions whose curves are not null-homotopic, we prove that graphicality at every time is equivalent to a uniform length bound as $t\to-\infty$, and that these properties hold whenever the length is $o(\sqrt{-t})$. Under an additional positivity condition on the linearized height equation, every such solution with bounded length is a family of slices. We derive backward convergence to a limiting circle from the length bound and prove slice rigidity by an $L^2$ estimate for the height perturbation.
item.dc:creator: Beomseok Goh, Taehun Lee

item.title: Pseudo-Calabi Flow on Toric Variety
item.description: arXiv:2610.34340v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we prove the long time existence of the pseudo-Calabi flow on a compact toric variety for any $T^n$-invariant initial K\"ahler metric. If the Mabuchi functional is proper modulo automorphisms, the flow converges exponentially to a constant scalar curvature K\"ahler (cscK) metric. In particular, this gives a flow proof that properness of the K-energy implies the existence of a cscK metric in the toric setting.
item.dc:creator: Junhao Tian, Kai Zheng

item.title: Existence of static axisymmetric solutions to the Einstein equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.34555v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct smooth Riemannian metrics and scalar potentials that are invariant under a circle action and satisfy the static Einstein equations with positive cosmological constant. The underlying compact three-manifold is a ball with two disjoint open balls removed. The potential (or lapse function) is positive in the interior and vanishes at the boundary, consisting of three non-degenerate horizons. The areas of the two inner boundary components are controlled by two arbitrary parameters, namely the masses of the black holes, which are taken to be sufficiently small and comparable. Each inner horizon radius scales linearly with the individual mass parameters, while the separation of their reference centers scales as the cube root of the total mass. These two scales are assumed to be sufficiently small at different rates, whereas the cosmological length remains fixed. The main analytical challenge is to control the linearized equation and the nonlinear remainder simultaneously near the shrinking horizons, between the centers and in the outer region. Weighted H\"older estimates quantify the growth of the inverse and show that the error of an approximation joining Kottler collars to de Sitter space is small enough to close a contraction argument. Namely, we solve a reduced elliptic Einstein equation that is endowed with two obstruction tensors; varying the two axial positions removes their coefficients. The contracted Bianchi identity and an energy estimate for an auxiliary vector field (Killing field) introduced by the projection to vanish. Finally, for a fixed cosmological constant, the intrinsic metric of one of the two boundary components is sufficient to determine a static solution with simply connected interior and non-vanishing boundary gradient, up to isometry and multiplication of the potential by a positive constant.
item.dc:creator: Philippe G. LeFloch, Luc Rozoy

item.title: Scattering for the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map and the Steklov spectrum
item.description: arXiv:2610.34588v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop scattering theory for Dirichlet-to-Neumann (DtN) maps on asymptotically conic, unbounded domains $\Omega\subset \mathbb{R}^d$, that are only Lipschitz inside a compact set and whose boundary extends to infinity. Specifically, we prove a limiting absorption principle and demonstrate existence of the scattering matrix. As an application of the theory, we show that the eigenvalues of Steklov-type problems on curvilinear polygons, $\mathcal{P}$, are well approximated by the eigenvalues of a Dirac operator on $\partial\mathcal{P}$ whose transmission coefficients between edges meeting at a corner are given by the scattering matrix for DtN maps on asymptotically conic domains associated to the corners. Up to an arbitrary loss in the power of the eigenvalue, the error in the approximation is optimal among all possible asymptotics that use only local information about $\partial\mathcal{P}$.
item.dc:creator: Jeffrey Galkowski, Marcello Malagutti, Ruoyu P. T. Wang

item.title: Uniform Large Deviations, Barrier Identity and the N\'eel--Arrhenius Law for the One-Dimensional Stochastic Landau--Lifshitz--Gilbert Equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.34823v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the one-dimensional stochastic Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation with a regularised, multiplicative, degenerate trace-class noise of strength sqrt(eps), the regularisation being Q_delta^{1/2} = (I + delta A^{beta/2})^{-1}, A = -d^2/dx^2, beta > 3/2, and determine the exponential rate of thermally induced magnetisation reversal. (i) Uniform large deviations at fixed delta: for every delta > 0 the solution satisfies a large deviation principle on C([0,T];H), with a good rate function, uniformly in the initial datum over a V-bounded set with compact H-closure; no non-degeneracy of the noise is assumed. (ii) Removal of the regularisation: as delta tends to 0 the noise tends to space-time white noise. With U_delta the state-space quasi-potential and U_0 that of the limiting control problem (Q_0^{1/2} = I), U_delta converges to U_0 in the Gamma-sense, and the barrier is delta-independent: the infimum of U_delta over the boundary of D equals that of U_0 and equals c_* times the infimum of the micromagnetic energy E over that boundary, c_* = 2 lambda_2/(lambda_1^2 + lambda_2^2), under two structural assumptions only and with no geometric or transversality input. Pointwise convergence fails, so the Gamma-limit is the sharp form of the statement. (iii) Neel-Arrhenius law: combining (i) and (ii) with the classical exit-time theorem, the escape time tau from D = {E < r} satisfies both levels of the law - for every fixed delta > 0, eps log E[tau] converges, uniformly on compact subsets of the initial set, to the barrier, and lim_{delta->0} lim_{eps->0} eps log E[tau] = c_* times the infimum of E over the boundary of D. The Arrhenius exponent is therefore stable under the regularisation of the noise and is determined by the micromagnetic energy alone.
item.dc:creator: Zdzis{\l}aw Brze\'zniak, Fan Gu, Liang Li

item.title: Genus Increase in Closed Mean Curvature Flows
item.description: arXiv:2610.35000v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct counterexamples to Ilmanen's genus-reduction conjecture for closed mean curvature flows. We prove that a compact hypersurface with a single isolated conical singularity and a power rate of convergence to its cone admits a mean curvature flow whose forward rescaled limit is a prescribed expander smoothly asymptotic to that cone. Combining this theorem with closed mean curvature flows with prescribed tangent flows (arXiv:2405.15577, arXiv:2607.23879) and the noncompact counterexample (arXiv:2605.09657) gives the desired examples.
item.dc:creator: Jingwen Chen

item.title: On Gill's problem with anomalous diffusion
item.description: arXiv:2610.35078v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The classical formulation of Gill's theorem establishing the linear stability of the buoyant flow in a vertical porous channel subject to transverse diffusion and bounded by impermeable walls is here reconsidered from the perspective of anomalous mass diffusion. Anomalous diffusion is a physical effect implying a more general formulation of the governing equations of mass transfer either in a fluid or in a fluid-saturated porous medium. Anomalous diffusion is mathematically modelled via a diffusion equation with a time-dependent mass diffusivity. In this study, the stationary and parallel buoyant flow in a vertical porous layer saturated by a fluid is investigated. The implications of the anomalous diffusion model for the proof that such a flow is always linearly stable are analysed.
item.dc:creator: A. Barletta

item.title: Instability of exact finite-amplitude acoustic-gravity waves
item.description:
arXiv:2610.35210v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Godin (	extit{J. Fluid Mech.}, vol. 767, 2015, pp. 52--64) showed that compressible fluids in a uniform gravity field support finite-amplitude incompressible wave motions, in which every parcel conserves pressure and density, and constructed exact Gerstner-type surface and edge waves, possibly carried by currents. Using the short-wavelength instability method for compressible flows, we show that these waves are linearly unstable above a critical steepness. The stability of each fluid level reduces to a Floquet problem depending on two parameters: the steepness $\mathfrak{e}=e^{ka_2}$ and $
u^2=(1-\mathfrak{e}^2)
u_0^2$, where $
u_0^2=\cos^2\alpha\,N_0^2/\Omega^2$, $N_0$ is the buoyancy frequency of the hydrostatic reference state, $\alpha$ the inclination of the plane of motion and $\Omega=(gk\cos\alpha)^{1/2}$ the intrinsic orbital frequency. In an isentropic fluid, a level is unstable if $\mathfrak{e}>1/3$, recovering Leblanc's threshold for Gerstner waves (	extit{J. Fluid Mech.}, vol. 506, 2004, pp. 245--254) and extending it to compressible surface and edge waves; weak stable stratification lowers the threshold to $ rac13- rac{32}{81}
u_0^2+O(
u_0^4)$. In an isothermal atmosphere, $
u_0^2=\kappa\cos\alpha/(kH)$, where $H$ is the pressure scale height. For horizontal wavelengths near $5.5\,H/\cos\alpha$, principal subharmonic resonance makes the critical steepness vanish. For the fast airglow wave observed by Hecht et al. (	extit{J. Geophys. Res.}, vol. 107, 2002, D20, 4444), which Godin interpreted with his solution, the lidar temperature places the layer in which this interpretation is consistent on this resonance, where the critical steepness is typically 0.1 instead of $1/3$. Instability is confined to a layer beneath the free surface of surface waves and to a wedge at the shoreline of edge waves.
item.dc:creator: Christian Puntini

item.title: At last, an explicit singular value decomposition for electrical impedance tomography
item.description: arXiv:2610.35217v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We derive a diagonalization of the normal operator of the linearized electrical impedance tomography (EIT) problem on the disk in the case of a radially symmetric Schr\"odinger potential with Dirichlet-to-Neumann data. The diagonalization is achieved by transforming the normal operator to the adjacent interval finite Hilbert transform which has a known spectral theory including a commuting differential operator. The normal operator in this case is not compact and the spectrum continuous.
item.dc:creator: William R B Lionheart, Michael Pidcock, Cristiana Sebu

item.title: Bach-flat metrics and global regularity of conformal structures
item.description: arXiv:2610.35257v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study global regularity properties of conformal structures on compact manifolds with applications to conformally invariant variational problems. We find sharp conditions ensuring that a manifold equipped with a Riemannian metric of Sobolev class is conformally diffeomorphic to a smooth one. In particular, we prove that $W^{2,q}$ Bach-flat four-manifolds with $q > 2$ are smooth up to conformal diffeomorphisms. We also solve the Yamabe problem for $W^{2,q}$ metrics with $q > 2$ on three-manifolds under a mild conformal condition.
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo Avalos, Albachiara Cogo, Andoni Royo Abrego

item.title: A Numerical Method for the Fractional Semilinear Calder\'on Problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.35299v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a finite element method for reconstructing a coefficient in a fractional semilinear equation from a single exterior measurement.
item.dc:creator: Mukul Dwivedi, Jesse Railo, Andreas Rupp

item.title: Determinants of Dirichlet and Neumann Laplacians on Constant Curvature Surfaces with Geodesic Polygonal Boundary
item.description: arXiv:2610.35383v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We express the zeta regularized determinants of the Dirichlet and Neumann Laplacians on compact Riemann surfaces with constant curvature metrics and geodesic polygonal boundary in terms of the Laplacian determinant on their closed conical doubles. The formulae apply without restrictions on the genus or number of boundary components. They involve explicit corner angle factors and a quotient of the Reidemeister and $L^2$ norms on the determinant line of cohomology. The proof combines a relative BFK gluing formula with the comparison theorem for analytic and combinatorial torsion on manifolds with boundary, due to L\"uck and Vishik. As an application, we give a rigorous proof of the Aurell-Salomonson formula for Euclidean polygons. We also obtain explicit determinants for spherical and hyperbolic triangles and certain other geodesic polygons from known formulae for their doubles.
item.dc:creator: Victor Kalvin

item.title: The quermassintegral inequalities for k-convex spiral-star-shaped domains
item.description: arXiv:2610.35394v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We extend the quermassintegral inequalities of our earlier work \cite{GuanLi2009} from star-shaped domains to a substantially broader class of domains in Euclidean space, which we call spiral-star-shaped. A smooth domain is spiral-star-shaped if its boundary satisfies \[ \langle X+A X,\nu\rangle>0 \] for some fixed skew-symmetric linear map $ A$, where $X$ is the position vector and $\nu$ is the outward unit normal. The vector field $X+A X$ is conformal Killing, with dilation component $X$ and rotational component $A X$; its trajectories combine expansion and rotation, giving rise to the spiral terminology. When $A=0$, it reduces to ordinary star-shapedness, while nonzero $A$ allows domains that are not star-shaped in the usual radial sense. For smooth $k$-convex spiral-star-shaped domains, we prove long-time existence and exponential convergence to a round sphere for a locally constrained inverse curvature flow. The positive spiral support function provides the geometric control needed to treat initial hypersurfaces that need not be star-shaped in the usual sense. Monotonicity of the quermassintegrals along the flow yields sharp quermassintegral inequalities in this enlarged class, with equality if and only if the domain is a ball.
item.dc:creator: Junfang Li

item.title: Thermosolutal Marangoni instabilities in a weakly viscoelastic falling film with soluble surfactant
item.description: arXiv:2610.35481v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We examine the linear stability and nonlinear evolution of a heated falling film containing a soluble surfactant and a weakly viscoelastic liquid. The stress response is described by the short-memory Walters model, while surface tension depends on temperature and surface concentration. An Orr--Sommerfeld analysis and its long-wave limit determine how elastic memory and the two Marangoni stresses enter the instability threshold. A five-field weighted-residual model is then derived to describe finite-amplitude disturbances. The bulk and surface transport equations are written with compatible fluxes, which conserve their combined projected surfactant inventory in a periodic domain. The numerical examples show that solutal Marangoni stress suppresses disturbance growth and reduces the amplitude of the nonlinear waves. Thermal Marangoni stress increases the maximum growth rate, although its effect on the width of the unstable wavenumber band is different. Elastic memory changes both the onset and the finite-wavelength response. The nonlinear profiles develop a main hump and capillary ripples, accompanied by variations in bulk concentration, surface concentration, and interfacial temperature. These results describe the competition between thermocapillary forcing, surfactant redistribution and elastic stress within the retained long-wave model. The larger elastic parameters are interpreted as formal predictions of the truncated constitutive equations, rather than as a controlled extension to strongly elastic flow.
item.dc:creator: Sanghasri Mukhopadhyay, Severine Millet, Bastien Di Pierro, Asim Mukhopadhyay

item.title: Local Algebraic Stability of Wasserstein Gradient Descent-Ascent and Mean Field Langevin Dynamics without Spectral Gap
item.description: arXiv:2610.35528v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the local stability of Wasserstein gradient descent-ascent (GDA) for entropy regularized two-player zero-sum games on noncompact domains. When one or both equilibrium measures fail to satisfy a Poincar\'e inequality, the spectral gap arguments underlying local exponential convergence are unavailable. we show that Wasserstein GDA converges algebraically to the mixed Nash equilibrium in chi-squared divergence, provided the initial relative density is a small perturbation in $L^2$ with bounded algebraic moments. The proof has two main ingredients: a cancellation in a negative Sobolev energy estimate, and a bootstrap argument that keeps the moments bounded uniformly in time. For polynomial-tailed equilibria, we construct perturbations supported far out in the tails that survive over diffusive time scales, which gives algebraic lower bounds on the worst-case relaxation rate. We also establish analogous local algebraic stability and lower bound results for mean-field Langevin dynamics, when the equilibrium fails to satisfy a spectral gap.
item.dc:creator: Jing An, Lihan Wang

item.title: Boundedness and continuity of phase-corrected gradients on Sobolev spaces
item.description:
arXiv:2610.35584v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a function $\psi: \mathbb{R}^d ightarrow \mathbb{C}$, we define the phase-corrected gradient $
abla_{\!\circ} \psi = |\psi|^{-1} \overline{\psi}\,
abla\psi$ and study the regularity of the map $\psi \mapsto 
abla_{\!\circ} \psi$ on Sobolev spaces. Since $\mathrm{Re}[
abla_{\!\circ} \psi] = 
abla |\psi|$, the phase-corrected gradient fits naturally into the framework of nonlinear composition operators. Its imaginary part $\Lambda = \mathrm{Im}[
abla_{\!\circ} \psi]$, on the other hand, plays a key role in quantum hydrodynamic models. We prove that $\psi \mapsto 
abla_{\!\circ} \psi$ is bounded and continuous from $W^{s,2}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ to $W^{s-1,2}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ for $1 \leq s <  rac32$, and we show that the threshold $s =  rac32$ is sharp. In particular, this answers an open question concerning the continuity of the map $\psi \mapsto |\psi|$ on Sobolev spaces. We also show that our results remain valid for functions that do not necessarily decay at infinity, a relevant setting in the context of Ginzburg--Landau theory. Finally, we extend our analysis to more general phase-corrected gradients of the form $f(|\psi|^{-1} \psi) 
abla \psi$, where $f: \mathbb{S}^1 ightarrow \mathbb{C}$ is Lipschitz, and discuss implications for certain parabolic PDEs.
item.dc:creator: Lars Eric Hientzsch, Raffaele Scandone, Robert Wegner

item.title: Index and nullity of critical spherical catenoids in hyperbolic three-space
item.description: arXiv:2610.35651v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that every critical spherical catenoid in a geodesic ball of hyperbolic three-space has Morse index four and nullity two. This resolves Medvedev's index conjecture throughout the parameter range of the catenoid family. The kernel consists precisely of the normal components of rotations that preserve the center of the ball and tilt the axis of the catenoid. As a consequence, the radius of the supporting ball increases strictly along the family. The proof combines a global boundary inequality obtained from a Wronskian, a positive Dirichlet eigenfunction supplied by the time component of the unit normal, and a Riccati comparison for the angular mode $k=2$. A ground-state identity then yields positivity of every angular mode $k\ge2$.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Dorofeev, Alexander Pigazzini

item.title: Morse index characterization of the Veronese projective plane
item.description: arXiv:2610.35820v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Following Simons' seminal work in 1968, every closed, connected, embedded minimal surface in the four-sphere that is not totally geodesic has Morse index at least five. In this paper, we prove that equality holds if and only if the surface is congruent to the Veronese projective plane. Relying on recent advances by Bernstein and Ketover, this characterization settles Kusner's 1996 conjecture on the minimizers of the Willmore functional in dimension four for surfaces whose normal bundle has nonzero Euler number. This is always the case, in particular, for embeddings of nonorientable surfaces whose orientation double cover has even genus.
item.dc:creator: Alessandro Carlotto, Yangyang Li, Zhihan Wang

item.title: Nonabelian Higgs fields from minimal submanifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.35837v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ Yang-Mills-Higgs fields on a broad class of noncompact Riemannian manifolds, concentrating in the large-mass limit along prescribed nondegenerate minimal submanifolds of codimension three. The solutions have uniformly bounded rescaled energy. On closed manifolds with $b_1(M)=0$, adding a suitably scaled Higgs potential gives an analogous concentration result. Our construction completes one direction of the correspondence proposed by Parise, Pigati and Stern, realising prescribed minimal submanifolds of codimension three as concentration sets of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ Yang--Mills--Higgs fields.
item.dc:creator: Marco Badran

item.title: Optimal tradeoffs between variance and sensitivity, via Hellinger-Kantorovich geometry
item.description: arXiv:2610.35858v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: While the goal of classical statistical theory is to minimize the variance of unbiased estimators, an additional goal of some recent research is to minimize or constrain other notions of the instability of estimators. In particular, a subset of the authors recently introduced a notion of instability termed "sensitivity", which represents the expected amount that an estimator would change if its inputs were infinitesimally perturbed. In this work, we study the multiobjective problem of minimizing both the variance and sensitivity over unbiased estimators in a given statistical model, and we aim to determine Pareto optimal tradeoffs between these two objectives. Our main results show that the Pareto front for these tradeoffs is precisely determined by endowing the statistical model with the Hellinger-Kantorovich geometry, which interpolates between the Hellinger and Wasserstein geometries that are known to be associated, respectively, with the separate minimization of variance and sensitivity. We also develop a $Z$-estimation technique which constructs estimators that asymptotically achieve Pareto optimal pairs of variance and sensitivity. While computing the Pareto front and constructing the resulting estimators in practice requires solving a continuum of partial differential equations, we fully execute this program in some parametric examples of interest where the analysis is already non-trivial. Our results also shed light on some classical statistical problems, for example by showing that the maximum likelihood estimator achieves the smallest asymptotic sensitivity among all estimators achieving the optimal asymptotic variance.
item.dc:creator: Adam Quinn Jaffe, Congwei Yang, Nicol\'as Garc\'ia Trillos, Bodhisattva Sen

item.title: Existence and Uniqueness of Local and Global Solutions for a Partial Differential-Algebraic Equation of Index One
item.description: arXiv:2411.15658v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we use the theory of nonlinear semigroups to establish the existence and uniqueness of both local and global solutions for a partial differential-algebraic equation (PDAE) of index one. This method is applied to a reaction-diffusion system coupled with an elliptic equation in one dimension by transforming the PDAE into a system of linear evolution equations with a Lipschitz-continuous perturbation
item.dc:creator: Seyyid Ali Benabdallah, Messoud Souilah

item.title: The monopolist's free boundary problem in the plane
item.description: arXiv:2412.15505v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the Monopolist's problem with a focus on the free boundary separating bunched from unbunched consumers, especially in the plane, and give a description of $C^{1,1}(\overline{\Omega})$ solutions for the family of square domains $\{(a,a+1)^2\}_{a \ge 0}$. The Monopolist's problem is fundamental in economics, yet widely considered analytically intractable when both consumers and products have more than one degree of heterogeneity. Mathematically, the problem is to minimize a smooth, uniformly convex Lagrangian over the space of nonnegative convex functions. What results is a free boundary problem between the regions of strict and nonstrict convexity. We study both the structure of the free boundary problem on convex domains in $\mathbf{R}^n$ showing that each bunch extends to this boundary and providing a proof in $\mathbf{R}^2$ that the interior free boundary can only fail to be smooth in one of four specific ways (cusp, high frequency oscillations, stray bunch, nontransversal bunch); in addition we offer a description of $C^{1,1}(\overline{\Omega})$ solutions to Rochet and Chon\'e's example on the family of squares $\Omega = (a,a+1)^2$, where we discover bifurcations first to targeted and then to blunt bunching as the distance $a \ge 0$ to the origin is increased. To do this, we extend the localization for measures in convex-order to accommodate potential discontinuities in the product allocation map at the fixed boundary. We also employ techniques from the study of the Monge--Amp\`ere equation and the obstacle problem.
item.dc:creator: Robert J. McCann, Cale Rankin, Kelvin Shuangjian Zhang

item.title: On the cutoff phenomenon for fast diffusion and porous medium equations
item.description: arXiv:2503.11770v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The cutoff phenomenon, conceptualized at the origin for finite Markov chains, states that for a parametric family of evolution equations, started from a point, the distance towards a long time equilibrium may become more and more abrupt for certain choices of initial conditions, when the parameter tends to infinity. This threshold phenomenon can be seen as a critical competition between trend to equilibrium and worst initial condition. In this note, we investigate this phenomenon beyond stochastic processes, in the context of the analysis of nonlinear partial differential equations, by proving cutoff for the fast diffusion and porous medium Fokker-Planck equations on the Euclidean space, when the dimension tends to infinity. We formulate the phenomenon using quadratic Wasserstein distance, as well as using specific relative entropy and Fisher information. Our high dimensional asymptotic analysis uses the exact solvability of the model involving Barenblatt profiles. It includes the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck dynamics as a special linear case.
item.dc:creator: Djalil Chafa\"i, Max Fathi, Nikita Simonov

item.title: Conformal Green functions and Yamabe metrics of Sobolev regularity
item.description: arXiv:2507.01674v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We provide a full resolution of the Yamabe problem on closed 3-manifolds for Riemannian metrics of Sobolev class $W^{2,q}$ with $q > 3$. This requires developing an elliptic theory for the conformal Laplacian for rough metrics and establishing existence, regularity and a delicate blow-up analysis for its Green function. Most of the analytical work is carried out in dimensions $n \geq 3$ and for $W^{2,q}$ Riemannian metrics with $q>\tfrac{n}{2}$ and should be of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo Avalos, Albachiara Cogo, Andoni Royo Abrego

item.title: Global well-posedness and asymptotic behavior of large strong solutions to the 3D full compressible Navier-Stokes equations with temperature-dependent coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2508.06933v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: It is well known that the global well-posedness of the Navier-Stokes equations with temperature-dependent coefficients is a challenging problem, especially in multi-dimensional space. In this paper, we study the 3D Navier-Stokes equations with temperature-dependent coefficients in the whole space. When the initial density and the initial temperature are linearly equivalent to some large constant states, we establish the first result on the global existence of large strong solution. Moreover, the optimal decay rates of the solution to its associated equilibrium are established when the initial data belong to $L^{p_0}(\mathbb{R}^3)$ for some $p_0\in[1,2]$.
item.dc:creator: Yachun Li, Peng Lu, Zhaoyang Shang

item.title: Abstract second-order boundary control systems
item.description: arXiv:2510.10363v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Many physical systems, such as vibrating elastic bodies, acoustic media and electromagnetic fields, are governed by second-order evolution equations $\ddot x+D\dot x+Sx=0$ and interact with their environment through their boundary. The classical analysis via the operator matrix $\mathcal{A}=\left[\begin{smallmatrix}0&I\\-S&-D\end{smallmatrix}\right]$ requires $S$ to be self-adjoint, which typically fixes a boundary condition a priori and thus excludes boundary control. We therefore use $S$ only to define the energy space and govern the dynamics by a maximal operator $S_{\max}\supset S$ whose domain carries no boundary condition. Based on a factorization $S=A^*A$, we construct a boundary triplet for the associated operator matrix and define boundary inputs and outputs of Robin type, parametrized by an operator $P$ on the boundary space. We show that the resulting system is impedance passive and internally well-posed if $P$ is a contraction, and that for $D=0$ this covers all boundary conditions under which the free dynamics generate a contraction semigroup.
