Moreover, we show that the position-momentum formulation (e.g., $\left[\begin{smallmatrix}0&I\\\Delta&0\end{smallmatrix}\right]$ for the wave equation) and the strain-momentum formulation (e.g., $\left[\begin{smallmatrix}0&\nabla\\\operatorname{div}&0\end{smallmatrix}\right]$) describe the same open system, including its boundary inputs and outputs. We illustrate our results by an $n$-dimensional wave equation and Maxwell's equations.
item.dc:creator: Till Preuster, Timo Reis, Manuel Schaller

item.title: Weakly localized states of one dimensional Schrodinger equations have localized energy
item.description: arXiv:2510.16283v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the asymptotics of the Schr\"odinger equation with time-dependent potential in dimension one. Assuming that the potential decays sufficiently rapidly as $|x| \to \infty$, we prove that the solution can be written as the sum of a free wave $e^{-it\Delta} u_+$ and a weakly bound component $u_{\text{wb}}(t)$. Moreover, we show that the weakly bound part decomposes as $u_{\text{wb}}(t) = u_{\text{loc}}(t) + o_{\dot{H}^1}(1)$, where $\partial_x u_\text{loc}(t)$ is localized near the origin uniformly in time. Since decay conditions on the potential do not preclude resonances unless $d \geq 5$, our results can be seen as a natural extension of [Terence Tao. Dynamics of Partial Differential Equations, 5(2), 2008] and [Avy Soffer, Xiaoxu Wu. arXiv:2304.04245] to the lower-dimensional case.
item.dc:creator: Gavin Stewart, Avy Soffer

item.title: Viability Theory in the 1-Wasserstein Space
item.description: arXiv:2511.19779v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article, we establish necessary and sufficient viability conditions for continuity inclusions over the 1-Wasserstein space. Depending on the regularity properties of the dynamics, we derive two results which are based on fairly different proof strategies. When the admissible velocities are Lipschitz in the measure variable, we characterise viability by the nonemptiness of the intersections of the velocity sets with the graphical derivatives of the constraint map. On the other hand, when the admissible velocities are merely upper semicontinuous in the measure variable, we provide a sufficient condition for viability involving the infinitesimal behaviour of their Aumann integral in time over a neighbouring set of measures.
item.dc:creator: Beno\^it Bonnet-Weill, Alberto Dom\'inguez Corella, H\'el\`ene Frankowska

item.title: Structured Continuity Equations in Fibred Wasserstein Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2511.19784v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article, we develop a comprehensive ODE-theory for structured continuity equations in fibred probability spaces, which represent a class of heterogeneous PDEs arising as the meanfield limit of nonexchangeable particle systems. After investigating in depth the topologies induced by the so-called fibred (or conditional) and classical Wasserstein metrics on such probability spaces, we establish quantitative Cauchy-Lipschitz and qualitative Carath\'eodory-Peano well-posedness results for structured continuity equations, along with precise correspondences between this class of evolutions, classical Lagrangian dynamics, and continuity equations. In keeping with what has long been known for exchangeable dynamics, we derive a general meanfield approximation result by solutions of nonexchangeable particle systems, along with a quantitative variant thereof under practically reasonable regularity assumptions on the driving field and initial data.
item.dc:creator: Beno\^it Bonnet-Weill, Nastassia Pouradier Duteil

item.title: The Bennati-Dragulescu-Yakovenko model in the continuous setting: PDE derivation and long-time behavior
item.description: arXiv:2512.06101v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this manuscript, we develop and analyze a continuous version of the well-known Bennati-Dragulescu-Yakovenko (BDY) dollar-exchange discrete model. Starting from the conservative BDY exchange mechanism, we rely on kinetic theory for multi-agent systems in order to propose an analogous Boltzmann-type continuous dynamics, which does not belong to the class of other popular kinetic models for wealth exchange. We employ the quasi-invariant limit procedure to rigorously derive a nonlinear PDE on the half-line, which is a Fokker-Planck equation featuring the boundary value in the drift term. The PDE is supplemented with a nonlinear Robin-type boundary condition encoding conservation of total agents and wealth. We prove relative entropy decay to the unique stationary state that is the Boltzmann-Gibbs (exponential) distribution with a $\mathrm{e}^{-c\sqrt{t}}$ convergence rate. We determine a new entropy production term which is a Fisher information minus a competing term which measures the temporal distance of the boundary term from its equilibrium value. Thanks to an inequality relating the Fisher information relative to the Boltzmann-Gibbs equilibrium to the $L^1$-norm, we prove $L^1$-convergence toward equilibrium and convergence of the boundary term (up to a subsequence), as well as convergence in both the Hellinger and Fourier distances. This represents an advancement in classical arguments of entropy decay for Fokker-Planck equations in a kinetic framework.
item.dc:creator: Fei Cao, Nadia Loy

item.title: Positive weak solutions of a double-phase variable exponent problem with a fractional-Hardy-type singular potential and superlinear nonlinearity
item.description: arXiv:2601.01346v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In the present paper, we study a double-phase variable exponent problem which is set up within a variational framework including a singular potential of fractional-Hardy-type. We employ the Mountain-Pass theorem and the strong minimum principle to obtain the existence of at least one nontrivial positive weak solution.
item.dc:creator: Mustafa Avci

item.title: On the Dirichlet boundary value problem on Cartan-Hadamard manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2601.09930v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study bounded solutions of Dirichlet boundary value problems for semilinear elliptic equations on Cartan-Hadamard manifolds with pinched negative curvature. We prove nonexistence when the asymptotic boundary has zero Hausdorff measure at an exponent determined by the upper curvature bound and the spectral parameter. The result holds for continuous viscosity solutions under a one-sided bound on the nonlinearity, including the Allen-Cahn equation. The proof combines convex barriers at infinity, distance comparison for $C^{1,1}$ hypersurfaces and a spectral maximum principle. For surfaces, no lower curvature bound is needed.
item.dc:creator: Marcos P. Cavalcante, Jos\'e M. Espinar, Diego A. Mar\'in

item.title: Improved well-posedness for the limit flow of differentiation of roots of polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2602.06826v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study the partial differential equation on the circle that was heuristically obtained by Steinerberger \cite{steinerberger2019nonlocal} on the real line and which represents the evolution of the density of the roots of polynomials under differentiation. After integrating the partial differential equation in question, we observe that it can be treated with the theory of viscosity solutions. This equation at hand is a non linear parabolic integro-differential equation which involves the elliptic operator called the half-Laplacian. Due to the singularity of the equation, we first restrict our study to strictly positive initial condition. We obtain a comparison principle for solutions of the primitive equation which yields uniqueness, existence, continuity with respect to initial condition. We then extend these results to general initial data. We finally prove that the system of particles on the circle introduced by Steinerberger indeed approximates the solution of the equation.
item.dc:creator: Charles Bertucci (CEREMADE), Valentin Pesce (CMAP)

item.title: Liouville phenomenon for the Klein-Gordon equation in 1+1 dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2603.03868v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the Klein-Gordon equation in one spatial and one temporal dimension. Physically, this equation describes the wave function of a relativistic spinless boson with positive rest mass. Mathematically, this is the most elementary hyperbolic partial differential equation, after the wave equation itself. Relative to the origin, the spacetime splits according to the light cones, and we find four quarter-planes, two of which are timelike while the remaining two are spacelike. Not unexpectedly, the solutions behave quite differently in the two types of quarter-planes. It turns out that the spacelike quarter-planes exhibit a Liouville phenomenon, where insufficient growth forces the solutions to display a certain kind of symmetry, where the values on the two linear edges are in a one-to-one relation. This phenomenon shares features with the classical Liouville theorem as well as the Phragmen-Lindelof principle for harmonic functions. We obtain sharp transition from uniqueness to nonuniqueness.
item.dc:creator: Haakan Hedenmalm

item.title: A heterogeneous nonlocal advection--diffusion system
item.description: arXiv:2603.17749v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a self-contained investigation of the local and global well-posedness of a system of nonlocal advection--diffusion equations for a heterogeneous population over $\mathbb{R}^d$, $d \in \mathbb{N}$. Each convolution kernel $K_{ij}$, which describes the nonlocal advection of species $i$ according to the distribution of species $j$, is assumed to have its own regularity $\nabla K_{ij} \in L^{q_{ij}}(\mathbb{R}^d)$, $1 < q_{ij} < \infty$. Local well-posedness of the mild solution and its regularity is obtained using semigroup theory and contraction mapping arguments. For kernels that satisfy a given interaction cycle condition, global existence is established using a Nash-type inequality to show an \textit{a priori} energy bound. For a class of kernels that need not satisfy the interaction cycle condition, a dynamical property satisfied by a normalised \(L^p\) norm of each species is used to obtain a uniform-in-time bound under a smallness condition on the initial data. An example family of kernels with varying regularities, supplemented by numerical simulations, is then considered to illustrate the theory developed in this work and how it may be generalised.
item.dc:creator: Joseph McCusker, John Christopher Meyer, Mabel Lizzy Rajendran

item.title: Finite-Time Weak Singularities and the Statistical Structure of Turbulence in 3D Incompressible Navier-Stokes Equations
item.description: arXiv:2603.28308v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper provides a rigorous mathematical analysis of the global regularity problem for the 3D incompressible Navier-Stokes (NS) equations, specifically addressing the conditions under which smooth initial data may lead to a loss of regularity. By departing from traditional phenomenological turbulence models and focusing strictly on the mechanical energy transport equation, we derive a fundamental critical condition, $\boldsymbol{u}\cdot\nabla E = 0,$ where $E = \frac12|\boldsymbol{u}|^2 + p$ is the specific mechanical energy, which characterizes the transition from laminar to turbulent flow.
item.dc:creator: Chio Chon Kit

item.title: Transition Time for Weak Singularities of the Navier-Stokes Equations
item.description: arXiv:2604.09640v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper constructs a rigorous mathematical framework for investigating laminar-turbulent transition induced by weak singularities of incompressible Navier-Stokes (NS) equations. By integrating the energy identity of Leray weak solutions with the singularity criterion $\left\lVert \boldsymbol{u} \right\rVert_{H_0^1(\Omega)}\to0$, a closed analytical form of the laminar-turbulent transition characteristic time is derived. The theoretical scaling $t_{\text{trans}}\sim\nu/U^2$ (equivalent to $t_{\text{trans}}\sim t_c/\text{Re}$) is verified to be consistent with classical experimental observations in shear flows. This work reveals that laminar-turbulent transition is dominated by the local regularity collapse of Leray weak solutions rather than global viscous diffusion, and provides a novel theoretical interpretation for the onset of turbulence from the perspective of NS equation weak singularities.
item.dc:creator: Chio Chon Kit

item.title: Numerical study of the 2D Kaup-Broer-Kuperschmidt Boussinesq system
item.description: arXiv:2605.05183v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work we consider the well posed version of the Kaup-Broer-Kuperschmidt system in two dimensions. We numerically construct soliton type solutions and show that they are unstable both against dispersion and singularity formation. Further, we study line solitons and their stability, as well as generally localised initial data. In either case we fail to find stable structures.
item.dc:creator: Th\'eo Gaudry, Christian Klein, Jean-Claude Saut, Nikola Stoilov

item.title: Quantitative Homogenization and Uniform Lipschitz Estimates for Lam\'e-Stokes Systems
item.description: arXiv:2606.05098v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study homogenization of Lam\'e-Stokes systems with fixed material parameters. Incompressible elastic inclusions are periodically distributed in a connected elastic matrix, with an elastic buffer near the outer boundary. The divergence constraint acts only in the inclusions, and the full pressure contributes to interface traction. We identify the effective elasticity system for the traction problem of period $\varepsilon$. Under the respective regularity assumptions, we obtain the optimal $O(\varepsilon)$ convergence rate for the displacement in $L^2$. For the unsmoothed first-order approximation, the displacement error in $H^1$ and the pressure error in $L^2$ over the inclusions are both $O(\varepsilon^{1/2})$. For a $C^{1,1}$ outer boundary, both errors improve to $O(\varepsilon)$ on every fixed interior subdomain. We establish local interface Schauder estimates including the full pressure and combine them with large-scale iteration to obtain Lipschitz estimates for the displacement up to the boundary and $L^\infty$ bounds for the pressure in the inclusions. These Lipschitz and pressure bounds are uniform in $\varepsilon$ for $C^{1,\kappa}$ interfaces and outer boundary and compatible $C^{0,\tau}$ traction data, where $0<\tau<\kappa<1$.
item.dc:creator: Beichen Wang

item.title: Invariant measures for the one-dimensional stochastic Navier-Stokes-Korteweg equations
item.description: arXiv:2606.07423v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the long-time behaviour of a one-dimensional compressible viscous fluid with general capillarity and density dependent viscosity, driven by a stochastic force. In particular, we prove the existence of invariant measures by applying the Krylov-Bogoliubov method in a setting where the dynamics is supported on a non-complete phase space. This analysis is further enhanced by the derivation of a refined stability result determining the continuous dependence with respect to the initial data. The present paper exhibits some properties and results for Korteweg fluids which are not known in absence of the capillarity tensor. In particular, we prove that the Markov semigroup associated with strong solutions is Feller and we can consider ranges of the adiabatic and viscosity exponents $\gamma$ and $\alpha$ larger than those available in the current ergodic literature for compressible fluids. Also the interplay between the choice of the physical domain and the use of a damping term is discussed.
item.dc:creator: Donatella Donatelli, Lorenzo Pescatore, Stefano Spirito

item.title: Survey on periodic vortex patches
item.description: arXiv:2607.12577v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This survey revisits classical results on the existence of periodic solutions in incompressible fluid dynamics. Owing to the breadth of the subject, we restrict our attention to the simplest and most illustrative framework: the two-dimensional Euler equations and vortex patch solutions. The aim is not to present new results, but rather to provide a unified and streamlined exposition of several classical constructions by combining ideas from the original works with more recent developments.
item.dc:creator: Claudia Garc\'ia

item.title: Asymptotic Geometry of Shifting Superlevel Sets for Elliptic Dirichlet Problems: Normal Decomposition, Geometric Energy, and Discrete Reflection Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2607.16912v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study elliptic superlevel geometry and return dynamics for the class $\mathcal{O}_{C}$. Let $C \subset \mathbb{R}^{N}$ be a compact strictly convex core, and $\Omega \in \mathcal{O}_{C}$ a bounded domain whose boundary is a global normal graph over $\partial C$ with inward normals returning to $\operatorname{int} C$. For $-\Delta u = f$ in $\Omega$ ($u=0$ on $\partial\Omega$), with $f \geq 0$, $f \not\equiv 0$, $\operatorname{supp} f \Subset \operatorname{int} C$, we analyze the superlevel sets $\Omega_{t} = \{u > t\}$ for $t \downarrow 0$. We prove that for small $t > 0$, $\partial\Omega_{t}$ is a global normal graph given by $\partial\Omega_{t} = \{c + d_{t}(c)\nu(c) : c \in \partial C\}$, satisfying $\|d_{t} - d_{0}\|_{C^{1}} = O(t)$ and $d_{t} = d_{0} - t b_{0} + o_{C^{1}}(t)$, where $b_{0}$ depends on the Hopf derivative and transversality. Using normal-graph formulas, we show $\Omega_{t} \in \mathcal{O}_{C}$. The return maps $F_{t} : \partial C \to \partial C$ are well-defined, satisfying $\|F_{t} - F_{0}\|_{L^{\infty}} = O(t)$ and $F_{t} = F_{0} + t \mathcal{A}_{0} + o_{L^{\infty}}(t)$. For any sequence $t_{n} \downarrow 0$, the non-autonomous system $x_{n+1} = F_{t_{n}}(x_{n})$ is asymptotically autonomous with background map $F_{0}$. These results bridge elliptic boundary-layer deformation and return-map dynamics relative to a convex core.
item.dc:creator: Mohammed Barkatou, Mohamed El Morsalani

item.title: A point-free theory of quantitative homogenization
item.description: arXiv:2608.05077v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a purely operator-theoretic framework for quantitative homogenization that bypasses the traditional reliance on large-scale spatial regularity and probabilistic assumptions. Inspired by Tartar's vision of a point-free theory, we derive explicit norm resolvent estimates using only the algebraic structure of multiscale operators and the abstract geometry of Hilbert spaces. In this framework, the effective macroscopic dynamics and the abstract corrector emerge naturally from an orthogonal decomposition of the state space, governed algebraically by a Schur complement. To quantify the convergence rate, we introduce a frequency-splitting technique and a flux corrector obtained by inverting the microscopic derivative on the residual field; this controls the error for regular macroscopic data in terms of explicit, $\varepsilon$-independent operator norms. This abstract perspective places on one footing stationary, non-stationary, periodic, quasi-periodic, and stochastic homogenization. We demonstrate that the physical distinctions between these media---and their respective convergence rates---are captured by the behavior of the spectral measure of the microscopic derivative operator, evaluated on the residual field, near zero frequency; in the periodic case the rate $O(\varepsilon)$ is proved, while in the stochastic case the rates are conditional on a density-of-states hypothesis. Furthermore, our results apply for multiscale systems that do not uphold subadditivity of energy quantities or do not have a well-defined Brillouin zone.
item.dc:creator: Thuyen Dang, Yuliya Gorb, Silvia Jim\'enez Bola\~nos

item.title: Two improved Liouville-type theorems for the 3D stationary tropical climate model without temperature assumptions
item.description:
arXiv:2608.13149v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we establish two improved Liouville-type theorems for the three-dimensional stationary tropical climate model without imposing any temperature assumptions. Compared with previous results, we achieve significant improvements on the growth assumptions imposed on $u$, $v$ and $
abla v$. Owing to the special structure inherent to the equations, we fully exploit the $L^2$-estimate for the oscillation of the temperature, refined interpolation techniques and an iteration argument to establish a Liouville-type theorem under flexible and relaxed power-law growth conditions. As an interesting consequence, we obtain the triviality of solutions under the integrability conditions imposed only on $(u,
abla v)$ or $(
abla u,
abla v)$. Furthermore, by developing a systematic framework to handle the energy function associated with the non-trivial solutions and with the aid of delicate ODE analysis and a contradiction argument, we refine our Liouville-type theorem by introducing logarithmic corrections to the growth rates.
item.dc:creator: Zhibing Zhang

item.title: Self-similar stationary Navier--Stokes flows in a half-space with arbitrarily large swirl forcing
item.description: arXiv:2608.25432v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study axisymmetric self-similar solutions of the stationary Navier--Stokes equations with $(-3)$-homogeneous forces and no-slip boundary conditions in a half-space. For a fixed force without swirl, we characterize the interval of amplitudes for which solutions exist and describe the velocity singularity at its finite endpoints. For each parameter in this interval, a solution exists after adding a swirl force of any size, and it is unique among solutions with bounded profiles when the swirl force is sufficiently small. The proof uses the nonnegative contribution of swirl to a Riccati equation and a comparison estimate. We also prove that, when the tangential curl of the force is sufficiently small, there exists a unique solution with small velocity profiles.
item.dc:creator: Yun Wang, Chunjing Xie, Shaoheng Zhang

item.title: The high dimensional monostable reaction-diffusion equation with free boundary and radial symmetry
item.description: arXiv:2608.25672v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the radially symmetric version of the reaction-diffusion equation $u_t-d\Delta u=f(u)$ with a monostable nonlinearity $f$, viewed as a model for the spreading of a species with population range $r<h(t)$ and density $u(t,r)$ ($r=|x|$), where the free boundary $r=h(t)$ is governed by $u(t,h(t))=\delta>0$ and $h'(t)=-d u_r(t,h(t))/\delta$. For the one-dimensional case ($N=1$), Du \cite{DN} proved that when $\delta\in(0,1)$, spreading occurs: $u\to1$ locally uniformly in $\mathbb{R}$, $h(t)\to\infty$, and $\lim_{t\to\infty}[h(t)-c_*t]=\tilde{h}\in\mathbb{R}$ with no logarithmic shift. In the present paper we consider $N\ge2$ and establish a complete trichotomy: spreading for $\delta\in(0,1)$; transition for $\delta=1$, where $u\to1$ uniformly on $[0,h(t)]$ and $h(t)\to h_\infty\in(0,\infty)$; and vanishing for $\delta>1$, where $h(t)\to0$ and $u\to\delta$ uniformly on $[0,h(t)]$. For the spreading regime, by constructing sharp upper and lower solutions, we prove that the solution converges globally to the semi-wave profile and reveal a logarithmic shift of the form $ \lim_{t\to\infty}\big[h(t)-c_*t+c_N(\delta)\log t\big]=\hat{h}\in\mathbb{R}$, with the coefficient $c_N(\delta)>0$ satisfying $ \lim_{\delta\to0}c_N(\delta)=d(N-1)/c_0$, where $d(N-1)/c_0$ is the shift coefficient for the high-dimensional radial pushed-case Cauchy problem. These results reveal the connection to the spreading behavior modeled by the corresponding Cauchy problem.
item.dc:creator: Hongkai Cao, Jingyi Cui, Chengzhe Tang, Xiaoyan Zhang

item.title: A quantitative convergence rate for torsional creep to the distance function as p tends to infinity
item.description: arXiv:2609.06534v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that the Dirichlet $p$-torsion function $u_p$ converges to the distance to the boundary $d$ at the rate $O(1/p)$ in the uniform norm, on every bounded domain and with a constant depending only on the dimension and the diameter. The upper bound comes from a radial barrier with its pole at a boundary point, which is an admissible comparison function for $p>n$ and needs no boundary regularity; the lower bound comes from an inscribed ball. On the ball the error equals $(1+\log n)/p+O(p^{-2})$, so the order $1/p$ cannot be improved in general. Under a uniform exterior ball condition an annular barrier gives $u_p\le K_\Omega^{1/(p-1)}d$ for every $p>1$, with $K_\Omega$ explicit in the dimension, the diameter and the exterior radius; on convex sets the constant is the diameter, and a multiple of $d$ is a supersolution whenever $-\Delta d$ has a positive distributional lower bound. On $C^2$ domains, the same barrier and the classical gradient maximum principle give $\norm{\nabla u_p}_{L^\infty}^{p-1}\le K_\Omega$. When $-\Delta d$ is a measure of finite total variation, which we prove for $C^1$ domains with a uniform exterior ball, the gradients converge in $L^q$ at the rate $O(p^{-1/2})$ for $q\le2$ and $O(p^{-1/q})$ for $q\ge2$; these exponents are not claimed to be sharp. The explicit ball profile shows that the gradients do not converge uniformly.
item.dc:creator: Farid Bozorgnia, Masoud Bayrami-Aminlouee, Khudoyor Mamayusupov

item.title: Asymmetric Periodic Water Waves in Finite Depth
item.description: arXiv:2609.08150v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the full two-dimensional water-wave equations in finite depth, with and without surface tension. Water waves have been studied mathematically for more than two centuries. Reflection symmetry remains a common assumption in constructions of periodic steady waves, although asymmetric profiles have been observed in experiments and numerical computations. We construct families of periodic stationary solutions whose free surfaces have no axis of reflection, in both the pure-gravity and capillary--gravity cases. To the best of our knowledge, this provides the first rigorous construction of asymmetric periodic pure-gravity waves for the full two-dimensional water-wave problem in finite depth. The proof combines localized vorticity laws with a Lyapunov--Schmidt reduction. In the pure-gravity case, we introduce a small background shear flow to obtain an invertible boundary operator and couple the interior and free-surface approximations at leading order.
item.dc:creator: Yuchen Wang, Shusen Yan, Maolin Zhou

item.title: Variational properties of Perron's extremal solutions in the Bernoulli one-phase problem
item.description: arXiv:2609.14981v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the Perron extremal solutions of the stationary one-phase Bernoulli problem. These solutions are important in several applications, but not much is known about the regularity of their free boundaries due to their non-variational construction. We show that, in fact, Perron extremal solutions retain some variational features; specifically, they are solutions in the sense of inner variations. We establish this property by showing that extremal solutions arise as infinite-time limits of monotone solutions of the parabolic Bernoulli problem. As a consequence, we are able to describe the structure of singularities for Perron extremal solutions in two dimensions: largest subsolutions have smooth free boundaries, while smallest supersolutions have free boundary points that are either smooth, or whose blow-up limits are two-plane wedges with equal slope.
item.dc:creator: Farhan Abedin, William M. Feldman, Kerrek Stinson

item.title: Isolated singularities of solutions to the Yamabe equation in higher dimensions I
item.description: arXiv:2609.28323v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We complete, in the general Riemannian setting, the classification of isolated singularities of positive solutions to the Yamabe equation for dimensions \(3\le n\le29\), initiated in the flat case by Caffarelli, Gidas, and Spruck in 1989. Precisely, every isolated singularity is either removable or the solution is asymptotic to a Fowler solution. The sharpness of this range is established by counterexamples for every dimension \(n\ge30\) in our companion paper.
item.dc:creator: Zheng-Chao Han, Qinfeng Jiang, Hua-Yang Wang, Jingang Xiong, Lei Zhang

item.title: Continuous Data Assimilation for Memristive FitzHugh--Nagumo Neural Networks
item.description: arXiv:2609.30480v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this study, we investigate continuous data assimilation for a class of partly diffusive FitzHugh--Nagumo neural networks with memristive feedback and linear synaptic coupling. The nudging algorithm implemented here only adds a feedback term to the membrane-potential equations, while the recovery and memductance variables remain unobserved. We obtain weighted energy estimates that give sufficient conditions for exponential convergence of the data-assimilated solution to the reference solution under full or coarse membrane potential observations. Moreover, we prove energy-class uniqueness in dimensions one and two. In dimension three, the uniqueness criterion is an \(L^4\) membrane-potential initial data. We also establish an observational-noise estimate for locally square-integrable forcing, yielding an asymptotic error bound when the noise energy is eventually bounded.
item.dc:creator: Jing Tian

item.title: Singular analysis of the principal eigenvalue for cooperative elliptic systems with drifts
item.description: arXiv:2609.32693v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We determine the small-diffusion limit of the principal eigenvalue for a one-dimensional cooperative elliptic system with component-dependent drifts and Neumann boundary conditions. For scalar equations, this limit is determined by local data at the drift equilibria and boundary points. We show that such localization fails for systems: switching between components can make some intervals spectrally relevant. We first prove that the logarithmic transforms of all component eigenfunctions converge to the same function, which solves a scalar Hamilton-Jacobi equation. The associated Aubry set determines the asymptotic behavior of the principal eigenvalue. Under nondegeneracy assumptions, this set decomposes into isolated points, regular intervals, and composite intervals containing common drift zeros. We then identify the effective value of each class through local Ornstein-Uhlenbeck spectra and interval transport problems, and establish that the limit of the principal eigenvalue is the minimum of these class values. A unique minimizing class also determines the common logarithmic eigenfunction profile.
item.dc:creator: Shuang Liu

item.title: Unique continuation, nonexistence and bubbling for the critical $p$-Laplace equation in the plane
item.description: arXiv:2609.34204v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For $1<p<2$ we prove weak and strong unique continuation properties for the solutions to $\Delta_pu+f(u)=0$ in a planar domain, with $f$ continuous and such that $|f(s)|\leq C|s|^{p-1}$: a solution vanishing on an open set vanishes identically, and so does a solution vanishing to infinite order at a single point. We can therefore make progress towards a proof of some long-standing nonexistence results available only for $p=2$, such as a celebrated one of Esteban and Lions, establishing here that for the critical $p$-Laplace equation with zero Dirichlet boundary condition on a half-plane, there are no nontrivial finite energy solutions. In the plane, unique continuation thus provides the missing ingredient for a generalisation to the $p$-Laplacian operator of a classical result of Struwe on the bubble-profile decomposition of possibly sign-changing Palais-Smale sequences associated to the Brezis-Nirenberg problem, which remains open in dimension $N\geq3$ for $p\neq2$. We obtain a characterisation of their loss of compactness in terms of the finite energy solutions of $\Delta_pu+|u|^{p^*-2}u=0$ in $\mathbb R^2$.
item.dc:creator: Carlo Mercuri

item.title: Normalised Hamiltonian Elliptic Systems: a Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality for bilinear mass
item.description: arXiv:2610.08774v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study Hamiltonian elliptic systems with prescribed bilinear mass $\int_{\mathbb{R}^N}uv=a>0$. We establish a Gagliardo--Nirenberg inequality in the crossed gradient pairing and bilinear mass, on scaling-invariant component-bounded classes. It identifies the critical curve $1/p+1/q=N/(N+2)$ and the restricted energy trichotomy. For power nonlinearities, we establish uniqueness up to common translations and nondegeneracy of positive profiles throughout the Sobolev-subcritical hyperbola. Exact scaling then classifies positive normalised solutions and identifies the unique critical mass. In dimension two, we develop a bilinear exponential Gagliardo--Nirenberg estimate with a sharp gradient threshold and a truncated scalar refinement with the optimal quartic leading coefficient. Adapting variational ideas from [Cassani-Tarsi, Calc.Var.PDE (2015)] we combine a mass-normalising quotient, reduction over the full negative fibres and compactness below the concentration threshold to obtain least-energy positive radial solutions for pure exponential nonlinearities at every prescribed mass below the cubic limiting mass. Local perturbative branches and a small-frequency exponential branch yield explicit mass-response formulas.
item.dc:creator: Daniele Cassani, Giulio Romani

item.title: Sharp noncommutative Hilbert and Riesz inequalities: classification and spectral corrections
item.description: arXiv:2610.10158v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For every $1<p<\infty$, with $p^*=\max\{p,p/(p-1)\}$, we determine the sharp Hilbert norm $C_p=\cot(\pi/(2p^*))$ on $L^p(\mathbb{R};\mathcal{S}_p)$ and the sharp uniform bound $D_p=\csc(\pi/p)$ for retained and strict Riesz projections of maximal subdiagonal algebras in finite tracial von Neumann algebras. The Hilbert value is also the common Fourier--Schur completely bounded norm. For finite matrices, a nonnegative logarithmic determinant defect connects Hein\"avaara's tracial joint spectral measure to eigenvalues. The resulting transfer identity classifies finite signed real ridge inequalities on nilpotents and identifies their least additive eigenvalue corrections. A dual theorem characterizes weak-* limits of weighted angular measures of finite nilpotents. In general finite tracial algebras, separate positive-kernel and sharp determinant-covariance comparisons yield the Riesz bounds. Consequences include the sharp Volterra constant, Riesz--Titchmarsh and shifted-transform formulas, joint real-pencil norms, and exact triangular and operator-valued Fourier Riesz norms.
item.dc:creator: Zhouyu Long

item.title: A Half-Space Theorem for the Allen--Cahn Equation in All Dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.15014v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that, in every dimension, a bounded, non-constant entire solution of the Allen--Cahn equation whose zero set is contained in a half-space is a one-dimensional heteroclinic solution.
item.dc:creator: Sanghoon Lee

item.title: Quantized slow blowup dynamics for the energy-critical Schr\"{o}dinger map flow
item.description: arXiv:2610.20313v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the Cauchy problem for the energy-critical Schr\"{o}dinger map into the 2-sphere: \[ \partial_{t}u = u\times\Delta u, \quad (t,x)\in\mathbb{R}^{1+2}, \quad u(t,x)\in\mathbb{S}^2 \] for equivariant initial data of homotopy degree $k=1$. Given any integer $L\in\mathbb{N}_+$, we exhibit a set of initial data arbitrarily close to the ground state harmonic map in the energy norm such that the corresponding solution blows up in finite time with a quantized rate \[ \lambda(t)\sim \frac{\left(T-t\right)^L}{\left|\log(T-t)\right|^{\frac{2L}{2L-1}}} \quad\mbox{as}\ \ t\uparrow T. \] Our proof is inspired by the techniques developed for the energy-critical harmonic map heat flow in a similar context by Rapha\"{e}l and Schweyer [Anal. PDE 7 (2014), 1713--1805]. However, its adaptation to a Schr\"{o}dinger-type equation requires the introduction of a new energy-Virial-Morawetz Lyapunov functional tailored to quantized slow blowup dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Jacek Jendrej, Jitao Xu, Xu Yuan, Lifeng Zhao

item.title: Structural stability of cylindrical transonic shocks to the three-dimensional Zeldovich-von Neumann-D\"oring combustion equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.25614v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We address the structural stability of transonic shock solutions to the Zeldovich-von Neumann-D\"oring (ZND) combustion equations in a cylindrical domain under three-dimensional perturbations of the incoming supersonic flow and exit pressure. The perturbed transonic shock is completely free and its strength and position are uniquely determined by the incoming flow and the exit pressure. The solution shares the same regularity for the velocity, the pressure, the entropy and the fraction of unburned gas. The main difficulties are that the shock front is a free boundary to be determined simultaneously with the subsonic flow and the equations for all states are coupled with each other due to the combustion process. One of the key ingredients of the analysis is to reformulate the three-dimensional ZND combustion equations into a deformation-curl system and four transport equations in terms of the deformation tensor and vorticity. Another one is an elaborate decomposition of the Rankine-Hugoniot conditions so that the shock front is uniquely determined by an algebraic equation and an unusual second order differential boundary condition is obtained on the shock front for the first order nonlocal deformation-curl system, from which an oblique boundary condition can be derived after homogenizing the curl system and introducing the potential function.
item.dc:creator: Zihao Zhang, Yan Zhou

item.title: Free boundary regularity for the porous medium equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.25740v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we resolve the local cone conjecture proposed by Kienzler, Koch, and V\'azquez concerning the free-boundary regularity of the porous medium equation. We prove that the local cone condition guarantees the smoothness of the free boundary lying outside the initial support. The proof relies on new gradient estimates obtained through maximum principle arguments and comparison principles. As an application, we establish the global-in-time smoothness of the free boundary for solutions with convex initial support under standard assumptions on the initial data.
item.dc:creator: Jiakun Liu, Junqing Wang, Maolin Zhou

item.title: Morse theory methods for a class of quasi-linear elliptic systems of higher order
item.description: arXiv:1709.02337v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop the local Morse theory for a class of non-twice continuously differentiable functionals on Hilbert spaces, including a new generalization of the Gromoll-Meyer's splitting theorem and a weaker Marino-Prodi perturbation type result. They are applicable to a wide range of multiple integrals with quasi-linear elliptic Euler equations and systems of higher order.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Calc. Var. Partial Differential Equations 58 (2019), no. 4, Paper No. 134
item.dc:creator: Guangcun Lu

item.title: Convergence of Quantum Lindstedt Series and Semiclassical Renormalization
item.description: arXiv:2301.12728v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this work we consider the KAM renormalizability problem for small pseudodifferential perturbations of the semiclassical isochronous transport operator with Diophantine frequencies on the torus. Assuming that the symbol of the perturbation is real analytic and globally bounded, we prove convergence of the quantum Lindstedt series and describe completely the set of semiclassical measures and quantum limits of the renormalized system. Each of these measures is given by symplectic deformation of the Haar measure on an invariant torus for the unperturbed classical system.
item.dc:creator: Victor Arnaiz

item.title: Monotonicity of the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of regular polygons
item.description: arXiv:2601.16285v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper we prove that the first Dirichlet eigenvalue $\lambda_1^N$ of an $N$-sided regular polygon of fixed area is a monotonically decreasing function of $N$ for all $N \geq 3$, as well as the monotonicity of the quotients $\displaystyle \frac{\lambda_1^{N}}{\lambda_1^{N+1}}$. This settles a conjecture of Antunes-Freitas from 2006 [P. Antunes, P. Freitas, Experiment. Math., 15(3):333-342, 2006].
item.dc:creator: Joel Dahne, Javier G\'omez-Serrano, Joana Pech-Alberich

item.title: Weak Singularity of Navier-Stokes Equations Based on Energy Estimation in Sobolev Space
item.description: arXiv:2603.07574v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Based on Dou Huashu's energy gradient theory, this paper focuses on the weak singularity of the incompressible Navier-Stokes (NS) equations in steady, fully developed flows. When the gradient of total mechanical energy is perpendicular to the streamline (i.e., $ u_j \frac{\partial E}{\partial x_j} = 0 $), substituting this critical condition into the NS equations with no-slip boundary conditions leads to the viscous term $ \nu \to 0 $. To rigorously analyze the regularity of the solution, Sobolev space $ H_0^1(\Omega) $ is introduced for energy estimation. The results show that the velocity field loses $ H^1 $-regularity, and the NS equations degenerate into Euler equations, which admit discontinuous weak solutions. Thus, the position where the mechanical energy gradient is perpendicular to the streamline becomes a weak singularity of the NS equations.
item.dc:creator: Chio Chon Kit

item.title: The estimates for Boolean surface area of polynomial threshold functions
item.description: arXiv:2604.08095v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Polynomial threshold functions (PTFs) are an important low-complexity class of Boolean functions, with strong connections to learning theory and approximation theory. Recent work on learning and testing PTFs has exploited structural and isoperimetric properties of the class, especially bounds on average sensitivity, one of the central themes in the study of PTFs since the Gotsman--Linial conjecture recently solved by OpenAI, \cite{GLsol}. In this work we study PTFs through the lens of the Boolean surface area (or Talagrand boundary) \[ \mathbf{BSA}[f]=\mathbb{E}|\nabla f|=\mathbb{E}\sqrt{s_{f}(x)}, \] a natural measure of vertex-boundary complexity on the discrete cube. Our main result is that every degree-$d$ PTF has polylogarithmic Boolean surface area: \[ \mathbf{BSA}[f]\le C_d(\log(en))^{C_d}. \] The proof is based on the PTF Restriction Lemma of Kabanets, Kane, and Lu \cite{KKL2017} and proceeds through a tail bound for the pointwise sensitivity. In particular, it controls all subcritical fractional moments of the sensitivity. We also record a random block partition principle for Boolean surface area and an alternative recursive argument following Kane's work \cite{DK} on average sensitivity, which independently yields the second bound \[ \mathbf{BSA}[f]\le \exp(C(d)\sqrt{\log n}). \] This bound was obtained in \cite{FSVZ} without clarifying the magnitude of $C(d)$, which we do below. For lower moments $\bE |\nabla f|^{\eta} \le C(d, \eta)$ there is no dependence on $n$ for $0<\eta <1$.

item.title: Long-time asymptotics of a full Camassa-Holm soliton gas
item.description: arXiv:2606.10727v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the long-time asymptotics of a full soliton gas for the Camassa--Holm equation. The analysis starts from a pure-soliton Riemann--Hilbert (RH) problem with \(2N\) poles and two distinct types of residue conditions. We prove that, as \(N\to\infty\), this discrete RH problem converges to a limiting soliton gas RH problem whose jump matrix contains two nonzero reflection coefficients. In this sense, the limiting problem gives a full soliton gas model for the Camassa--Holm equation, in contrast to the previously studied half soliton gas models, whose jump matrices involve only one nonzero reflection coefficient. The limiting RH problem is analyzed by the Deift--Zhou nonlinear steepest descent method. The presence of two nonzero reflection coefficients requires two different types of triangular factorizations of the jump matrix and leads to a more delicate \(g\)-function mechanism. The main difficulty lies in the construction of suitable \(g\)-functions adapted to the Camassa--Holm phase, together with the precise control of their behavior near the distinguished point \(k=i/2\) and at infinity. Depending on the location of the spectral endpoints \(\eta_1\) and \(\eta_2\), different \(g\)-function mechanisms arise. In this paper, we focus on Case I and derive the long-time asymptotic formulas in three elliptic-wave regions of the self-similar plane. In each region, the leading term is given by a finite-gap elliptic function, while in the central region the first correction is of order \(\mathcal O(t^{-1/2})\) and involves parabolic cylinder functions.
item.dc:creator: Dedi Yan, Xianguo Geng, Minxin Jia

item.title: Failure of the local decay formula for Arnold multiplicities under twisted K\"ahler--Ricci flow
item.description: arXiv:2608.30302v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Di Nezza--Guedj--Lu asked whether local Arnold multiplicities under maximal weak twisted K\"ahler--Ricci flow with fixed cohomology class satisfy $\lambda(\varphi_t,x)=\max\{\lambda(\varphi_0,x)-t,0\}$. We construct counterexamples with analytic initial singularities in every dimension $n\ge2$. On the Hirzebruch surface $\mathbb F_e$, $e\ge2$, the initial current $[S]+(e+1)[F]$ yields $\lambda(\varphi_t,x)=1/2-t/e$ for $x\in S\setminus F$ and $0<t<e/2$, where $S$ is the negative section and $F$ a fibre. Products with smooth stationary factors give higher-dimensional examples. The Zariski negative part of $\{S\}+\{F\}$, the reduced support class, forces extra divisor mass. For pure divisorial data with simple normal crossings support, a smooth semipositive representative of the reduced support class's positive part gives exact short-time formulas. On one surface we construct flows with identical initial current germs, background data and global initial Arnold multiplicity, but different local rates.

item.title: Symmetry-breaking in a discrete-choice LQG mean field game
item.description: arXiv:2610.05730v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Mean-field games provide a continuum framework for modeling the dynamics of large, interacting populations of non-cooperative agents. This paper studies symmetry-breaking in a finite-horizon, two-choice min-LQG mean-field game in which identical agents with linear stochastic dynamics choose one of two equally desirable terminal destinations, while trading off control effort against social pressure to conform. The model has an odd symmetry between the two destinations and therefore always admits a symmetric, dynamic Nash equilibrium in which the population splits evenly between them, producing a deadlock collective state at final time. Numerical studies have suggested that, as the penalty for social nonconformity increases, this symmetric equilibrium loses stability as a fixed point of an associated scalar, self-consistency map, and asymmetric consensus Nash equilibria emerge, where most agents select the same destination. By analyzing the linearized forward-backward PDE system through the scalar map representation, we provide a proof of this loss of stability of the symmetric equilibrium. Together with the odd symmetry of the map, this implies the existence of symmetry-broken mean-field game equilibria corresponding to consensus on either destination.

item.title: Higher-Order Paracontrolled Calculus for Geometric Rough Paths
item.description: arXiv:2610.17307v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the rough differential equation $$ \frac{du_t}{dt}= F(u_t) \zeta_t, \ \ u(0) = u_0 \in \mathbb{R}^d, $$ where $F : \mathbb{R}^d \to L(\mathbb{R}^d, \mathbb{R}^d)$ is a sufficiently regular vector field, and the noise $\zeta$ is a distribution in $\mathscr{C}^{\alpha-1}(\mathbb{R})$ for $\alpha \in (\frac{1}{4}, \frac{1}{3})$. We construct solutions to this equation at lower regularity than previous work of Gubinelli-Imkeller-Perkowski and Pr\"omel-Trabs using ideas from the high-order paracontrolled viewpoint of Bailleul-Bernicot. The key tool in our work is the development of a harmonic-analytic framework for proving a set of iterated commutator estimates which are necessary for the solution theory. We also show the procedure of enhancement when the noise $\zeta = dZ$, where $Z$ is a realization of fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter $H \in (\frac{1}{4}, \frac{1}{3})$.
